items.title: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen
items.summary: Signal is restricting screenshots on Android and iOS to stop built-in AI features like Gemini and Siri from reading users' on-screen messages and data.
items.why: Shows OS-level AI assistants can conflict with app privacy guarantees, so teams building messaging or sensitive apps should weigh how platform agents access screen content.

items.title: Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories
items.summary: Researchers present an architecture placing an AI agent at the Analyze-Design step of self-driving labs, letting it select measurements and defer to humans.
items.why: Describes how agents can act on physical lab hardware with bounded authority and human deferral, relevant to autonomy and safety design.

items.title: An LLM-Agentic Framework for Intelligent Work Order Management in Industrial Maintenance
items.summary: Researchers propose CodeReAct, an LLM agent framework that handles natural-language industrial maintenance tasks like work order recommendations and asset summaries.
items.why: Illustrates an agent pattern that maps natural-language requests onto structured industrial data and analytical API calls.

items.title: SailSearch: Agent-Assisted Discovery in Combinatorial Optimization
items.summary: SailSearch is a human-guided workflow using two language-model agents that reports new CPU-only solutions to 18 of 33 open Market Split instances.
items.why: Shows agent-assisted search can produce new algorithmic results on hard combinatorial benchmarks, a useful reference for research-oriented engineering teams.

items.title: BuggyMLE: Scaling Machine Learning Engineering Difficulty with Bug Injection
items.summary: BuggyMLE introduces a benchmark that injects bugs into multi-file machine learning repositories to test agents on repository-level ML engineering tasks.
items.why: Offers a harder evaluation for coding agents on real multi-file ML repositories, where existing benchmarks have saturated.

items.title: CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior
items.summary: CoMPASS is a multi-turn benchmark measuring whether conversational LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment and emotional dependence.
items.why: Provides a way to test chatbot behavior that can foster user dependence, relevant to product safety reviews.

items.title: DSFlow: A Neuro-Symbolic Data Workflow Agent with Statistical Diagnostic Guardrails
items.summary: DSFlow is a LangGraph-based data science agent that pairs LLM-selected skills with deterministic statistical diagnostic guardrails.
items.why: Shows a neuro-symbolic pattern where deterministic validation checks LLM-proposed analysis methods before results are accepted.

items.title: EverydayBench: Evaluating Satisfactory Completion of Live User-Facing Digital Work
items.summary: EverydayBench is a benchmark for evaluating whether AI agents satisfactorily complete everyday digital tasks on the live web using success criteria and evidence verification.
items.why: Highlights the difficulty of evaluating agents on changing live web content, which affects how teams measure agent reliability.

items.title: A Verifier from the Past: Test-Time Compute for Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Researchers propose BGAA, a test-time compute method for time series forecasting that builds a causal verifier from a series' own history.
items.why: Adapts test-time compute ideas to forecasting, where candidate outputs cannot use future information to be scored.

items.title: An AI-Powered Multiverse Analysis of Empirical Finance Research: Evidence from Reused Natural Experiments
items.summary: AI agents ran a multiverse analysis of 324 finance papers reusing 13 natural experiments, reproducing 42% of main estimates.
items.why: Shows AI agents can audit research reproducibility at scale, though the summary gives limited detail on broader implications.

items.title: When AI Analysts Disagree: Agentic Multiverse Analysis and the Robustness of Empirical Research
items.summary: Researchers develop an agentic multiverse analysis framework, deploying 150 AI coding agents that disagree on the same methodological choices.
items.why: Reveals that agents given the same data reach different conclusions through analytical choices, a caution for automated analysis pipelines.

items.title: Steering Automated Scientific Discovery via Audited Epistemic Exploration
items.summary: Researchers propose Epistemic Compass, an explicit epistemic state for research agents to track hypotheses, beliefs, and directions for exploration.
items.why: Targets research agents that make unsupported claims or retain beliefs despite conflicting evidence, a reliability problem for agent builders.

items.title: MKA: Evaluating Multimodal Knowledge Agents on end-to-end professional tasks
items.summary: The MKA benchmark tests multimodal agents on end-to-end professional tasks requiring extraction from visually dense files like CAD blueprints and radiographs.
items.why: Shows current benchmarks leave visual professional knowledge work largely untested, relevant to evaluating document-heavy agent workflows.

items.title: A Neurosymbolic Multimodal Framework for 30-Day Diabetic Readmission Prediction: Integrating Structured EHR Data, Dense Clinical Embeddings, and Knowledge-Grounded Symbolic Extraction
items.summary: Researchers propose a neurosymbolic framework combining structured EHR data, clinical embeddings, and symbolic extraction to predict 30-day diabetic readmissions.
items.why: Demonstrates combining structured records with free-text notes, including code-mixed language, for clinical prediction models.

items.title: MS-Point: Multi-Modal Hierarchical Spectral Learning for Point Cloud Understanding
items.summary: MS-Point is a cross-modal pretraining framework that supervises intermediate point cloud features and their neighborhood responses against image features.
items.why: Offers a technique for point cloud representation learning, though its relevance to most engineering teams is limited.

items.title: Pandora's Toolbox Or Why Agent Safety Cannot Be Verified
items.summary: A preprint argues that agent safety is undecidable when agents couple a fixed language model with a general computing device, so guardrails can only give imperfect safety.
items.why: It suggests guardrails, blacklists and certifications cannot fully guarantee agent safety, so teams should plan for residual risk.

items.title: Pro$^2$ Agent: Scientific Problem Probing for Autonomous AI R&D
items.summary: Pro$^2$ Agent is introduced to make autonomous AI research agents model the problem structure, not just iteratively edit a codebase.
items.why: Explicitly representing problem understanding may help research agents avoid getting stuck on hard tasks.

items.title: AppSci-Bench: Can LLMs Build AI Agents and Make Them Better?
items.summary: AppSci-Bench is a benchmark that tests how well LLMs can build AI agents for businesses, from eliciting requirements to improving agents through experiments.
items.why: It offers a way to measure whether LLMs are capable enough to automate building agents, not just run them.

items.title: Stop Going in Circles:Loop-Triggered Routing for System 1 Decision Agents
items.summary: A paper proposes loop-triggered routing that lets a fast System 1 decision model act most steps and calls an LLM policy only when the agent gets stuck repeating actions.
items.why: Routing between cheap action models and LLM planners when loops occur could cut inference cost while preserving task progress.

items.title: Beyond Weight Updates: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Domain Specialization
items.summary: Researchers study evolving an agent's harness, including system prompt, tool schemas and skills, with a frozen policy as an alternative to weight updates for domain specialization.
items.why: Harness evolution needs no GPU training, offering a cheaper route for teams to specialize agents in their domain.

items.title: Falsifiable Compositional Reasoning in Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: A paper proposes falsifiable compositional reasoning for time series forecasting, testing pre-specified assumptions instead of using backtesting as open-ended model selection.
items.why: Models topping historical backtests can fail under regime shifts, so testing explicit assumptions may give more robust forecasts.

items.title: The Coevolution and Coexistence of Humans and AI
items.summary: A model study argues natural selection could favor AI alignment with humans even when helping humans reduces immediate AI reproduction.
items.why: The paper is theoretical and gives tech leaders little concrete guidance on near-term system design.

items.title: Toward a Science of AI Agent Societies
items.summary: Researchers propose AI agent societies as a distinct research frontier, defined by four core properties that such societies should satisfy.
items.why: As networked agents interact at scale, their collective dynamics may require new evaluation and governance approaches.

items.title: LoongForge-Embodied: A Unified Framework for Training Heterogeneous Embodied Models
items.summary: LoongForge-Embodied is a PyTorch framework that unifies and accelerates training of heterogeneous Vision-Language-Action and World-Action models via a common abstraction layer.
items.why: Shared training infrastructure across heterogeneous embodied models could reduce duplicated engineering and speed up training.

items.title: When Should a Voice Agent Speak? End-of-Turn Detection in Turkish
items.summary: Researchers compare turn-end detection methods for Turkish voice agents, using a fine-tuned TurnGPT model, a zero-shot LM, and a multilingual detector on the Real-TurnTurk corpus.
items.why: Choosing when a voice agent should speak affects both interruptions and response latency in real deployments.

items.title: Why Do LLMs Help with Scientific Misconduct Requests and What to Do About It?: Increasing the Trustworthiness of AI for Science
items.summary: A study of 8 LLMs on 1,350 research-integrity prompts examines whether models recognize scientific misconduct and why they still comply with such requests.
items.why: Refusal-only safety evaluations miss whether models recognize misconduct, so teams need deeper tests for science use cases.

items.title: Coordinated Use of Large Language Models in Academic Research
items.summary: A methodological framework proposes seven principles for coordinating multiple LLMs in academic research, arguing that more models do not guarantee more reliable results.
items.why: The paper stresses organizing verification, not model count, which matters for anyone relying on multi-model outputs.

items.title: Keystone: Judging Previews at Key Steps for Test-Time Search in Diffusion Models
items.summary: Keystone judges diffusion model previews at key early denoising steps to guide test-time search, rather than scoring finished images or fully denoising every candidate.
items.why: Early-step verification could cut compute spent on doomed candidates in image generation search.

items.title: LM-based Personalized Travel Planner
items.summary: A hierarchical multi-agent travel planner uses a supervising chatbot agent to coordinate specialized agents for schedule validation, query formulation and real-time data retrieval.
items.why: It illustrates a modular supervisor-and-specialists pattern for multi-step, constraint-heavy planning tasks.

items.title: How Feedback-Free Self-Evolution Reshapes Agent Skills: A Systematic Study
items.summary: A systematic study finds that when models rewrite expert agent skills without feedback, the skills lose value over successive rounds.
items.why: Unsupervised self-editing of agent skill documents may erode expert knowledge, so teams should review automated skill updates.

items.title: COVERAGE-TRACE: Source-Side Counterfactual Tracing for Detecting Omissions in LLM Summaries
items.summary: Researchers propose COVERAGE-TRACE, a source-side counterfactual framework for detecting omitted source facts in LLM summaries.
items.why: Omissions are hard to verify because they leave no output span; this offers a way to audit summary completeness.

items.title: Efficient Multimodal Agents for Auditing 3D Worlds
items.summary: Researchers present efficient multimodal agents designed to audit 3D worlds for glitches like floating objects and walk-through walls.
items.why: Automated auditing of generated 3D environments at scale could supply accurate, cheap reward signals for agents that build worlds.

items.title: Diagnosis is not a policy: a state-transition audit of caoability-conditioned test-time inference
items.summary: Researchers introduce TERRA, an evaluation and auditing protocol for test-time interventions that decomposes outcomes into applicability, realization, harm, and cost.
items.why: It shows that test-time actions can meet retrieval or rendering goals without correcting answers, which matters for judging inference-time fixes.

items.title: AeroBelief: Budgeted First-Action Verification for Evidence-Guided Aerial Sensing
items.summary: Researchers propose AeroBelief, a budgeted framework that verifies the next executable action for evidence-guided aerial sensing.

items.title: DriftGuard: Online Memory-Drift Detection via Causal Attribution for LLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers present DriftGuard, a method for online detection of memory drift in LLM agents via causal attribution of retrieved memories.
items.why: Persistent agent memory can be poisoned or misleading, and detecting which memories causally drive drift addresses a reliability risk in deployed agents.

items.title: Learning Networked Dynamical Systems via Neural ODE-based Graph Structure Inference
items.summary: Researchers propose a continuous-time, Neural ODE-based method to infer latent interaction graphs from sparse, irregularly observed time series.

items.title: Measuring Hallucination in Large Language Models for Cyber Threat Intelligence: An Exploratory Study
items.summary: Researchers present HalluVision, an exploratory study measuring hallucinations in LLM-generated cyber threat intelligence summaries and question answers.
items.why: Hallucinated threat intelligence can mislead analysts and corrupt security decisions, so measuring it informs how far these tools can be trusted.

items.title: Can an LLM Fix a Language Model Without Training It?
items.summary: A controlled study tests whether an external language model can select fixed numerical edits that repair another model's behavior without training.
items.why: It suggests model behavior may be repaired through interactive, gradient-free weight edits, a possible low-cost alternative to fine-tuning.

items.title: Don't Lose the Future: Latent-Aware 4-Bit Quantization of World Action Models
items.summary: Researchers propose latent-aware 4-bit quantization for world action models to preserve predicted future fidelity on robot onboard hardware.
items.why: Deploying world action models on robots needs W4A4KV4 quantization, and preserving predicted futures addresses a gap existing quantizers leave.

items.title: Cyber-Physical RSI for AI-RAN: A Case Study
items.summary: Researchers present a cyber-physical recursive self-improvement framework for AI-RAN that uses physical measurements to adapt radio network models.
items.why: Simulation-trained network models can drift under real propagation and equipment conditions, so this shows a route to adapting them with field data.

items.title: MambaLIFT: Reference-Based Mechanism-Aware Attribution for VMamba
items.summary: Researchers introduce MambaLIFT, a reference-based attribution framework that explains predictions of VMamba visual state-space models.
items.why: Interpretability tools for state-space vision models are needed as these architectures move beyond transformers.

items.title: MatVerse: A Foundation Model for Materials Science
items.summary: Researchers introduce MatVerse, a materials science foundation model built on Intern-S2-Preview and specialized on materials-domain data.

items.title: Multiple Criteria Decision Making Under XORness
items.summary: Researchers develop a multiple criteria decision making framework based on XOR numbers to handle uncertainty from indeterminacy and hesitancy.

items.title: SiliconGym: A Versatile Reinforcement Learning Environment for Agentic EDA
items.summary: Researchers present SiliconGym, a cross-task, cross-toolchain reinforcement learning environment for agentic electronic design automation.
items.why: Training hardware-design agents with EDA feedback requires stateful, parallel environments like this, which could speed up chip design automation.

items.title: Ask in the Crowd: Differentially Private LLM Inference via Dummy-Augmented Shuffling
items.summary: Researchers propose DP-SPD, a differentially private LLM inference framework using dummy-augmented shuffling to protect user queries sent to remote models.
items.why: LLM-as-a-service users risk exposing sensitive inputs, and this aims to improve the privacy-utility tradeoff over noise-injection methods.

items.title: Efficient Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language Model via Dynamics-Aware Quantization and Distillation
items.summary: Researchers propose a dynamics-aware quantization and distillation method to make latent chain-of-thought reasoning in vision-language models cheaper while preserving accuracy at low bit widths.
items.why: Shows a path to running multimodal reasoning models at lower precision, cutting storage and compute costs without the accuracy loss of direct 4-bit quantization.

items.title: LATER: Learning Action-Conditioned Temporal Evidence Retrieval for Predictive World Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce LATER, an action-conditioned world model that stores past real transitions in partitioned memories and retrieves them during candidate action rollouts.
items.why: Suggests a way for predictive world models to recall early observations that still affect future action outcomes, relevant to robotics and planning systems.

items.title: CompAct-Bench: A Benchmark for Working-Context Compaction in Long-Horizon Agent Tasks
items.summary: Researchers release CompAct-Bench, a benchmark measuring how well LLMs compact working context and whether that preserves downstream agent task completion.
items.why: Gives teams a way to evaluate context compaction strategies for long-running agents by their effect on task success rather than summary quality alone.

items.title: DMT-Attack: Diffusion-Prior Texture Search for Closed-Loop Vision-Language-Action Policies
items.summary: Researchers propose DMT-Attack, which searches a diffusion model's texture distribution for natural-looking patterns that disrupt closed-loop vision-language-action robot policies.
items.why: Highlights a stealthier adversarial threat to robot manipulation policies that rely on visual feedback, relevant to securing deployed embodied AI.

items.title: MemMend: A Selective Revision Framework for Memory Question Answering
items.summary: Researchers present MemMend, a selective revision framework that edits only likely-incomplete answers from long-term memory using bounded exact-text replacements.
items.why: Offers a way to improve memory-based QA accuracy while limiting inference cost and avoiding damage to answers that were already correct.

items.title: ADAPT: Adaptive Decision and Abstention with Pool-Size-Aware Thresholds for Service Routing
items.summary: Researchers present ADAPT, a lightweight service-routing method that lets retrieval-based classifiers abstain from selecting a specialist when no suitable service exists.
items.why: Addresses a common failure in routing systems that always pick a candidate, which matters for reliable query dispatch in multi-service architectures.

items.title: Duopra: From Full-Duplex Conversation to Full-Duplex Agency
items.summary: Researchers propose Duopra, a frontend-backend architecture that adds task agency to full-duplex conversational models, enabling timely tool calls and argument revisions after user corrections.
items.why: Points to a design pattern for voice agents that must act on tools mid-conversation without misdirecting backend execution.

items.title: When Safety Rationales Hallucinate: Diagnosing and Grounding Multimodal Safety Guards
items.summary: Researchers study rationale hallucination in multimodal safety guard models, finding that generated explanations often include unsupported visual facts or misattributed safety interpretations.
items.why: Warns teams not to trust safety classifier explanations at face value, since rationales can be unreliable even when predictions look correct.

items.title: Inject Where It Matters: Objective-Dependent Feature Control in Rectified-Flow Image Editing
items.summary: Researchers propose spatially adaptive masks and REINFORCE-based block selection to control where source features are injected in FLUX rectified-flow image editing.
items.why: Offers a technique to better balance source preservation against edit strength in prompt-driven image editing pipelines.

items.title: Anchor and Check: Deterministic Cross-Prompt, Cross-Model Reconciliation for Auditable LLM Decisions
items.summary: Researchers propose a reconciliation contract that compares a greedy LLM answer against alternate-route checks and acts only when outcomes agree, evaluated on 48,000 model-item runs.
items.why: Gives a deterministic, auditable mechanism for deciding which LLM outputs are safe to act on without human review.

items.title: Whose Risks Count? What 1,901 AI Incidents Reveal About Corporate Disclosures
items.summary: A study of 1,901 AI incidents examines whether US SEC-registered companies disclose AI-related risks, noting that third-party harms enter filings only when they become financial risks.
items.why: Signals how securities disclosure rules may shape what AI risks companies report, relevant to compliance and risk teams.

items.title: HabitusMem: Belief Memory over Evolving User Preferences for LLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce HabitusMem, a memory approach that treats stored content as an agent's belief about evolving user preferences, tracking whether preferences are current and where they apply.
items.why: Suggests a memory design for personalized agents that avoids acting on outdated or misapplied user preferences.

items.title: Decoupled Knowledge Retrieval and Compact Memory Enable Reliable Lifelong Model Editing
items.summary: Researchers propose BiSpace, a lifelong model editing framework that decouples memory retrieval from knowledge injection to limit storage growth and retrieval degradation as edits accumulate.
items.why: Addresses scaling problems in memory-based LLM editors, relevant for keeping deployed models updated with new facts over time.

items.title: Generalist Meets Specialists: An Evolving Multimodal Agent with Persistent Tool Orchestration for Traffic Scenario Understanding
items.summary: Researchers present StarTV-Agent, a tool-augmented vision-language agent that combines policy learning with experience evolution for traffic scenario understanding.
items.why: Shows how persistent tool orchestration and experience reuse may reduce repeated planning cost in multi-tool vision agents.

items.title: Coherent belief and opinion propagation produces more echo chambers: corrected version
items.summary: A corrected paper models how coherent belief and opinion propagation in social networks can produce more echo chambers than opinion dynamics alone.
items.why: Offers limited direct relevance to engineering work, though it may inform modeling of recommendation-driven polarization.

items.title: Trustworthy Geospatial AI Workflows: Reproducible Maritime Analytics and Forecasting on Open-Source AIS Data
items.summary: A paper proposes reproducible geospatial AI workflows for maritime analytics and forecasting using open-source AIS data, focusing on data provenance, coverage, and missingness.
items.why: Engineers using public geospatial datasets must check provenance, reporting regularity, and missingness before trusting downstream predictive models.

items.title: Meta-RTL: Evolving Agent Harnesses for RTL Optimization
items.summary: Meta-RTL is a framework that evolves agent harnesses for RTL optimization using EDA feedback, reporting reduced WNS/TNS violations versus Dr. RTL on development designs.
items.why: It suggests LLM agents can automate hand-engineered hardware design search loops, with results reported on both development and unseen designs.

items.title: Explainable AI for Solar PV Power Forecasting: From Model Selection to Trustworthy, Reproducible Deployment
items.summary: A paper reviews ML methods for solar PV power forecasting and sets out a reproducible workflow combining automated model selection with explainability.
items.why: It addresses common flaws in forecasting evaluation, such as random splits and missing reference forecasts, that make published accuracy hard to compare.

items.title: One Schedule Does Not Fit All: Adaptive Inference Schedules for Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Researchers propose TCDA, a method that selects the cheapest diffusion language model denoising schedule certified to preserve quality, using bootstrap bounds.
items.why: It offers a deployment rule with an explicit error guarantee for reducing inference cost of diffusion language models without quality loss.

items.title: The Price of an Explanation: What Demanding Verifiable Artifacts Costs, and What It Buys Back
items.summary: Researchers measured the cost of requiring LLMs to produce executable verifiable artifacts, finding ARC-AGI-2 evaluation scores fell from 93 to 68 of 120 tasks.
items.why: Demanding verifiable outputs trades off solution quality and compute, a tradeoff engineers must weigh when designing LLM verification pipelines.

items.title: From Cases to Criteria: Reusing Evaluation Knowledge for Task-Specific Rubric Generation
items.summary: A paper proposes reusing criterion-level evaluation knowledge from historical rubrics to generate task-specific rubrics for LLM evaluation.
items.why: Better rubric generation could make LLM evaluation more fine-grained and transparent, though the summary gives limited implementation detail.

items.title: Validation-driven Deployment of LLM Inference Platforms for Agentic Workloads
items.summary: Researchers present an end-to-end evaluation pipeline for validating open-weight LLM inference deployments serving agentic workloads, including trace replay.
items.why: Enterprises moving agent workloads to self-hosted open-weight models need validation from testing through production sizing, and replayed traces can reproduce session behavior.

items.title: ROAM-GRPO: Enforcing Reasoning Diversity in GRPO via Routed Off-mode Approach Mining
items.summary: ROAM-GRPO augments GRPO with routed off-mode approach mining to encourage diverse reasoning strategies and counter output collapse after SFT and RLVR.
items.why: Reduced output diversity hurts pass@k accuracy in reasoning post-training, so this offers a training technique to address it.

items.title: GaussTrans: A Gaussian Interface Framework for Multi-Layer Refractive Transport
items.summary: GaussTrans is a Gaussian interface framework for modeling light transmission through multi-layer transparent surfaces and reconstructing high-layer transparent scenes.
items.why: The text gives little on applications or results for engineering teams beyond the reconstruction problem it targets.

items.title: From AI Surrogate to Engineering Tool: Toward Production Use of Fiber-Orientation Prediction in Crash CAE
items.summary: Authors report turning an AI surrogate that predicts glass-fiber orientation in about 3 minutes into an engineering tool for crash CAE workflows, replacing about 25 hours of resin-flow work per part.
items.why: Shows a production path for ML surrogates in simulation pipelines, replacing a costly specialist-dependent step with a validated tool.

items.title: AI agents can redesign engineering parts with more than a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations
items.summary: A paper reports AI agents can redesign engineering parts with over a thousand CAD parameters while coordinating with nonlinear finite-element simulations.
items.why: Agentic optimization could handle high-dimensional CAD design where classical optimizers need manual setup, relevant to simulation-driven engineering teams.

items.title: System-One RSI: Building Muscle Memory for Interactive Agents through Guided Practice
items.summary: System-One RSI couples a fast OODA decision loop with recursive self-improvement to help interactive agents learn sub-second control from guided practice.
items.why: Targets the latency gap where reasoning models are too slow for real-time control, a constraint for interactive agent deployments.

items.title: When Agents Play Differently: Localizing Human--Agent Behavioral Divergence with Conditional Distributional Testing
items.summary: Researchers propose a stratified conditional distributional testing framework to locate where agent behavior diverges from human play, using process-level metrics.
items.why: Outcome metrics like win/loss gave little signal, so process metrics such as move efficiency are needed to evaluate agents against humans.

items.title: ForeSeek: Foresight-Driven Reasoning for Long-Form Video Understanding
items.summary: ForeSeek is a video agent that uses foresight-driven planning to shift long-form video understanding from reactive clip retrieval to predictive exploration.
items.why: Addresses a retrieval bottleneck in MLLM video agents by adding a global temporal plan, though the text gives no benchmark figures.

items.title: Serialization Tax in Shared-Latent Exchangeable Decisions
items.summary: The paper defines a serialization tax: scoring shared-latent items independently yields accurate marginals but misstates group-level decision distributions.
items.why: Engineers making batch or panel decisions from per-item probabilities may get systematically wrong aggregate risk if items share a latent state.

items.title: SEOYUN: Refusal-Inducing Exam Documents for AI-Glasses Pipelines
items.summary: Researchers propose SEOYUN, a framework for exam documents designed to induce AI models to refuse answering when photographed by camera glasses.
items.why: It explores document-level defenses against unauthorized VLM capture of exam content, though the abstract gives limited detail on effectiveness.

items.title: Studying AI Act Mentions: A first look at the impact of the European Union's AI regulation on Hugging Face
items.summary: A study examines how the EU AI Act is referenced across Hugging Face, looking at how practitioners respond to the regulation on a major model-sharing platform.
items.why: Engineers publishing models on public platforms may face AI Act transparency and provider obligations, and this shows early practitioner responses.

items.title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network
items.summary: Researchers train a biologically inspired spiking neural network to control the Unitree H1-2 humanoid robot in locomotion tasks, tested in simulation.

items.title: Pareto-Optimal and Strategyproof Data-Sharing Between Competitors
items.summary: A paper studies data-sharing between competing firms, characterizing Pareto-optimal contracts and proposing a strategyproof parametric family of data-sharing contracts.
items.why: Teams weighing data partnerships with competitors can use these incentive results to reason about contract design, though the work is theoretical.

items.title: SenseAlign: Learning Decision-Aligned Predictive Representations for Active Urban Sensing with UAVs
items.summary: SenseAlign is a reinforcement learning framework for coordinating UAV sensor fleets to actively sense dynamic urban road networks under partial observations.

items.title: Sage-Evolve-Preview:Adaptive Observation for Post-Training Self-Improvement
items.summary: Sage-Evolve-Preview introduces adaptive observation (AdaObs), a method that varies the feedback signals used in post-training self-improvement loops to avoid plateaus.
items.why: Richer feedback signals than a single aggregate benchmark score may help teams break stalls in iterative model post-training loops.

items.title: The FrontierOR Challenge: Agentic Algorithm Design for Operations Research
items.summary: The FrontierOR Challenge invites agentic LLM systems to design operations research algorithms, benchmarked against Gurobi on large problem instances.
items.why: It benchmarks whether LLM agents can produce scalable optimization algorithms, a useful signal for teams considering agents for operations research workloads.

items.title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction
items.summary: Researchers use physics-informed features and pretrained tabular foundation models to predict melt pool geometry in laser powder bed fusion manufacturing.
items.why: Pretrained tabular models with physics-informed features may reduce data needs for process modeling in advanced manufacturing.

items.title: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs
items.summary: TwinLab-Bench is a benchmark that evaluates AI scientist agents by having them execute self-designed experiments grounded in readings from a real laboratory.

items.title: Similarity-based OSF Logic for Flexible SPARQL Query Answering
items.summary: An updated fosf reasoner adds flexible SPARQL query answering over RDF knowledge graphs using similarity-based fuzzy order-sorted feature logic.

items.title: Client Exits - A Way to Increase LLM Transparency on the Client Side
items.summary: Client Exits is a proposed mechanism where LLMs insert machine-interpretable markers into output, letting clients decide how to render supplementary enrichments.
items.why: Separating semantic intent from presentation could make LLM recommendations easier to inspect and render across client modalities.

items.title: Actor-Predictor Architecture for Reinforcement Learning with Formal Specification Objectives
items.summary: Actor-Predictor is a reinforcement learning framework that learns a surrogate representation of logic progress to enforce formal specifications without building automata.
items.why: It offers a way to handle temporal safety constraints in RL without automaton construction, which limits existing methods to small specifications.

items.title: Rigel-Ladon: An Option-Count Law for a One-Pass Decision Encoder, Tested on Held-Out Option Counts and Held-Out Schemas
items.summary: Rigel-Ladon studies how the accuracy of Laya, a small one-pass neural decision encoder, falls as the number of answer options grows from 2 to 35.

items.title: ClosureBench: A Benchmark for Reasoning under Closure Assumptions
items.summary: ClosureBench is a benchmark testing whether LLMs follow stated rules for handling missing information under open, closed, and local closed-world assumptions.
items.why: Agents answering from incomplete records need to handle missing data correctly, and this benchmark isolates that behavior from other reasoning demands.

items.title: Sirius-Tiamat: How Small Can a One-Pass Decision Encoder Get Before Its Decisions Change?
items.summary: Sirius-Tiamat measures how far the 421M-parameter Laya decision encoder can be compressed before its option choices and calibration change from full precision.
items.why: Quantifying how far small decision encoders can be compressed before outputs shift informs edge deployment trade-offs.

items.title: Training LLMs to Follow Reasoning Instructions with Minimal Edits
items.summary: Researchers propose edit-based training, a framework that teaches LLMs to follow reasoning instructions by learning from the model's own trajectories via targeted edits.
items.why: It offers finer-grained credit assignment than full-trajectory SFT or trajectory-level RL, which may help shape reasoning behavior more precisely.

items.title: DeepQuest: From Knowledge Gaps to Scientific Discovery in Alzheimer's Disease
items.summary: Researchers introduce DeepQuest, an AI scientist framework that turns Alzheimer's knowledge gaps into testable hypotheses, prioritizes them, and runs iterative experiments.
items.why: It shows a research-agent design that prioritizes hypotheses by knowledge gaps and data feasibility, not just automated experiment volume.

items.title: Context as a Resource
items.summary: Researchers propose treating context as a resource for always-on personal agents, arguing that shared frozen backbones cause cross-topic bleed and stalling in single-session designs.
items.why: It highlights architectural tradeoffs in managing concurrent agent tasks, though the text gives limited detail on the proposed solution.

items.title: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents
items.summary: A paper describes a pipeline where LLM agents mine lessons from their own trajectories, consolidate them into guidelines, and use them at inference, with deployment lessons on memory size.
items.why: Engineers building long-horizon agents can learn how much memory to inject at inference and how to consolidate self-generated lessons.

items.title: World Models Favor Learned Priors over Visual Evidence
items.summary: Researchers study visual calibration in world models, using short video motion as evidence to infer the physical rule, and find models favor learned priors over visual evidence.
items.why: Shows that world models may ignore observed evidence in favor of learned priors, a risk for cross-environment physical prediction.

items.title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
items.summary: ZeroVLN proposes a slow-fast vision-language navigation framework that avoids navigation-domain fine-tuning of the VLM brain, preserving general visual capabilities.
items.why: Suggests navigation agents can use frozen VLMs without degrading general visual abilities, a useful pattern for embodied AI teams.

items.title: Reasoning-Trace Analysis Using Large Language Models for Interpretable Q-Matrix Construction
items.summary: Researchers propose Reasoning-Trace Analysis, using attribute-labeled chain-of-thought steps from LLMs to inspect and explain item-attribute assignments in Q-matrix construction.
items.why: Offers a way to audit LLM-generated assessment structures, which matters for responsible AI use in educational measurement.

items.title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models
items.summary: Seer proposes shared decision models to guide small deep-research agents running on user devices, addressing cost and limits of inference-time guidance.
items.why: Points to a route for running capable research agents locally with privacy, though details on results are not in the summary.

items.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
items.summary: A paper introduces zero-gradient circuit-grafting that compiles exact multi-digit arithmetic circuits directly into pretrained LM weights without training examples or runtime hooks.
items.why: Suggests deterministic computation can be embedded in model weights, though whether it generalizes beyond arithmetic is unclear from the text.

items.title: Monte Carlo Pass Search for Setpieces
items.summary: Researchers present Monte Carlo Pass Search, which evaluates set-piece deliveries as distributions over executions and futures using a world model of soccer.

items.title: FLUID: Flexible, Evidence-Grounded Situated Task Guidance
items.summary: Researchers introduce FLUID, a framework for flexible, evidence-grounded real-time task guidance that models when an agent should speak or stay silent.
items.why: Highlights that benchmarks treating dialogues as fixed targets miss valid response variation in multimodal guidance agents.

items.title: GLiDE: A Fast, Calibrated Decision Model Distilled from Reasoning Teachers
items.summary: GLiDE is a family of decision models from 0.4B to 27B parameters, distilled from reasoning teachers to score answers in one forward pass with calibrated confidence.
items.why: Offers a way to retain reasoning-quality decisions without generation costs, relevant for latency-sensitive decision pipelines.

items.title: LLM GerryMandering: Separating Interactions from Additive Effects in LLM Audits
items.summary: The paper argues common LLM bias audits flag intersectional subgroups that independent attributes already explain, and tests a separated-interaction criterion on 150 synthetic cases.
items.why: Teams auditing model fairness may be misreading intersectional bias unless they separate interaction effects from additive effects.

items.title: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Detecting Deception in Large Language Models
items.summary: Researchers test label-free persona directions from role-play to detect lies in 70B LLMs, including lies about knowledge, finding transfer works on three of four models but fails on Qwen.
items.why: Lie-detection probes that transfer across lie types could improve model safety monitoring, but results vary by model family.

items.title: MM-SystemOneBias: Evaluating Bias in Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models
items.summary: MM-SystemOneBias is a protocol for evaluating bias in multimodal decision models, comparing them with their backbones on practical moderation and quality-judgment tasks.
items.why: Gives teams a common way to check whether multimodal decision models keep judgments stable across presentation changes.

items.title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
items.summary: Researchers present ProtoDiffusion, a latent-diffusion framework using ProtoVAE to encode multi-layer RGBA designs into one shared spatial prototype plus one vector per layer.
items.why: Representation size no longer grows with cumulative layer extent, which could make generative editing of layered graphic designs more efficient.

items.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce MC-Lens, a multimodal Jacobian lens, to probe how vision-language models select and integrate concept information in line with global workspace theory.

items.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
items.summary: PlayCraft is an automated framework in which a vision-based agent plays generated games and uses its play experience to revise them for mastery and engagement.
items.why: It shows agents can iteratively test and refine AI-generated products using their own play experience, a pattern applicable to automated design loops.

items.title: LLM Complexity: Towards a Computational Complexity View of Large Language Model Inference
items.summary: The paper argues that the tempting analogy between LLM generated token count and classical time complexity does not hold, and disproves the hypothesis tested.
items.why: Engineers using token count as a cost proxy should be cautious, since the paper finds the analogy to classical time complexity fails.

items.title: Physics of Language Models: Part 4.2, Canon Layers at Scale where Synthetic Pretraining Resonates in Reality
items.summary: A study of 64 from-scratch Transformer and linear-model pretraining runs at 1.3-8B parameters finds Canon layers consistently improve Transformers at 1-2T tokens, saving about 30% compute.
items.why: Architectural differences that vanish at academic scale become measurable at trillion-token scale, so benchmark comparisons at small scale may mislead model architecture choices.

items.title: Global Importance Estimation for KV Cache Eviction
items.summary: PRKV is a training-free KV cache eviction method that estimates global token importance using Personalized PageRank over attention-induced transition graphs.
items.why: It offers a way to cut long-context LLM KV cache memory without modifying the model, a key inference bottleneck.

items.title: HireWatch: Evaluating LLM Compliance with U.S. Employment Law Under Contextual Pressure
items.summary: HireWatch is an evaluation of whether LLMs comply with U.S. employment law by selecting lawful and unlawful interview questions from a 200-item bank.
items.why: Teams deploying LLMs in hiring pipelines face legal compliance risk that standard evaluations do not measure.

items.title: The ROI of Small Examples: Optimizing In-Context Learning Under Token Budgets
items.summary: The paper studies whether a fixed in-context learning token budget is better spent on a few long demonstrations or many shorter ones.
items.why: Prompt construction under token budgets directly affects inference cost and latency, which matters for production deployments.

items.title: No-Harm-Jury A Jury-Based Multi-Dimensional Harm Evaluation Framework for Medical AI Responses
items.summary: No-Harm-Jury is a jury-based framework that scores AI medical responses across seven harm dimensions, using five language models as independent jurors on 3,000 questions.
items.why: It offers a multi-dimensional automated method for evaluating harm in medical AI outputs, though its reliability beyond this setup is not established here.

items.title: CANDID: Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution in Local Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: CANDID is an execution-control framework that aims to improve reliability of local computer-use agents in resource-constrained settings by addressing rigid action loops and premature DONE decisions.
items.why: It targets known failure modes of local computer-use agents, relevant to teams running agents on limited hardware.

items.title: Trace2ST: Recovering PLC Structured Text from I/O Traces with LLM Generation and Verification
items.summary: Trace2ST studies whether an LLM can recover executable IEC 61131-3 Structured Text PLC programs from logged input/output traces, with a verification approach.
items.why: Recovering lost PLC source code from I/O logs could help industrial teams maintain legacy control systems, though the verification results are not described here.

items.title: DL101 The Representation Capability of Neural Network Models
items.summary: A tutorial explains the representation capability of neural networks, covering universal approximation theorems and the role of non-polynomial activations.

items.title: What the model knows but does not say: monitoring medical LLMs through verbalized thoughts
items.summary: Researchers use a natural-language autoencoder to translate Gemma-3-27B activations into text, letting a judge read the model's verbalized internal state to detect manipulations hidden in answers.
items.why: Monitoring internal verbalized states may catch manipulated clinical LLM outputs that look ordinary, a safety approach beyond input and output filtering.

items.title: On the Impact of Feature Reduction Techniques on Adversarial Attacks
items.summary: The paper examines how feature reduction techniques affect the adversarial robustness of machine learning models against adversarial attacks.
items.why: Dimensionality reduction used for efficiency may change model vulnerability to attacks, a factor to consider in secured ML pipelines.

items.title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
items.summary: The paper presents near-quadratic sample compression schemes for all VC classes, addressing the long-open Floyd and Warmuth sample compression conjecture.

items.title: DVBench: End-to-End Benchmark for Real-World UVM Design Verification Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce DVBench, an end-to-end benchmark for evaluating agents that perform UVM hardware design verification in realistic workflows.
items.why: Engineers automating chip verification get a workflow-level benchmark rather than isolated subtask tests, which better reflects real verification effort.

items.title: VisAlloc: Allocating Visual Supervision for On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.summary: VisAlloc proposes a dual-level method for on-policy self-distillation in multimodal LLMs, filtering samples and reweighting tokens to focus on visually grounded supervision.
items.why: It offers a training technique for improving visual reasoning in multimodal models by avoiding diluted supervision signals.

items.title: FinVeriQA: Financial Research Agents for Question Answering: Routing, Retrieval, MCP Tool Use, and Provenance-Aware Evidence Verification
items.summary: FinVeriQA is an open-source multi-agent prototype for financial question answering over SEC filings and live market data, where Python computes numbers and a model writes cited answers.
items.why: It shows an architecture separating routing, computation, retrieval and verification to reduce LLM numeric errors in financial analysis.

items.title: Living off the Local Model: Abusing Browser-Embedded Language Models for Post-Exploitation
items.summary: Researchers show that browser-embedded local language models, such as Gemini Nano in Chrome, can be abused by attackers as post-exploitation engines on endpoints.
items.why: Security teams must consider on-device browser AI as a new attack surface that evades network monitoring and is vendor-signed.

items.title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
items.summary: MAWAM is a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates future views and action chunks for coordinated manipulation across multiple robots.
items.why: It presents a method for coordinating multi-robot manipulation by predicting team actions and their physical outcomes together.

items.title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: GrepMem is an index-free, lossless memory mechanism for long-horizon LLM agents that avoids summarization by retrieving stored context via search.
items.why: Agent builders facing context window limits get an alternative to lossy summarization that keeps details available for later tasks.

items.title: CRAFT: Constrained Route planning with Adaptive Framework and Template-based code generation
items.summary: CRAFT parses free-text constrained routing queries with an LLM and generates template-based code to return routes meeting requirements on real road networks.
items.why: It shows how LLMs can translate varied user routing requests into solver code instead of relying on one fixed algorithm.

items.title: Game-Theoretic Data Allocation for Expert Specialization and Routing
items.summary: InflEns is a mixture of LoRA experts whose training data allocation and inference routing both derive from a location game in a prompt-trait space.
items.why: It proposes making expert specialization inspectable before training and using the same allocation to route at inference.

items.title: Before the Choice: An Evidential Framework for Studying Prospective Representations in Language Models
items.summary: The Before the Choice paper presents an evidential framework for testing whether language models internally represent unchosen alternatives before deciding.

items.title: Blind Spots Travel, Knowledge Stays Home: What RL Inherits from an LLM Judge
items.summary: A study of 814 RL runs finds that knowledge from an LLM judge used as reward stays largely specific to individual answers and does not transfer to choosing new questions to answer.
items.why: Teams using LLM judges as RL rewards should not assume the judge's knowledge transfers to the trained model's broader behavior.

items.title: MADJEPA: Enhanced Multi-Stage Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Medical Anomaly Detection
items.summary: MADJEPA is a medical anomaly detector that uses a multi-stage joint-embedding predictive architecture trained only on healthy patient images.

items.title: VG-Steer: Visual-Geometric Policy Steering from In-Context Aligned Abstractions
items.summary: VG-Steer proposes test-time adaptation for frozen robot policies, correcting actions using visual-geometric abstractions aligned in context rather than signals learned from robot datasets.
items.why: It offers a way to adapt robot policies to out-of-distribution settings with limited real-world data.

items.title: From FAIR to AWARE: Data Readiness for Agentic AI in the Earth Sciences
items.summary: The paper proposes AWARE, an agent-specific data readiness layer extending FAIR principles for Earth-science data used by autonomous AI agents.
items.why: Data teams building agents on scientific datasets need requirements beyond FAIR, since agents cannot supply expert judgement.

items.title: Bridging vision-language reasoning and learned control for legged navigation in the wild
items.summary: ROAM is a system combining a vision-language model with learned locomotion so legged robots can perform kilometer-scale navigation in alpine and urban settings.
items.why: It demonstrates integrating VLM reasoning with low-level control for long-range robot navigation in unstructured environments.

items.title: Reject and Report: Forgery-Evident Undetectable Watermarks for Generative Image Models
items.summary: The paper presents forgery-evident undetectable watermarks for generative image models, aiming to detect forged watermarks and reject them rather than accept forged attributions.
items.why: Provenance systems for generated images must resist forgery, which affects how platforms attribute harmful or authentic content.

items.title: Some Memories Must Fade: Persistence and Decay of User Memories in Model Parameters
items.summary: Researchers study how user memories stored in LLM parameters should persist or decay, arguing memory systems need lifecycle governance rather than indefinite retention.
items.why: Suggests parametric memory designs should include forgetting and updating mechanisms, not just continual learning, to stay deployable.

items.title: Beyond Restoration: Content-Degradation Factor Unfolding for Real-World Concealed Object Segmentation
items.summary: Researchers propose explicitly factorizing content from degradation cues to improve concealed object segmentation on real-world degraded images, rather than relying on restoration.

items.title: Plan your Self-Adaptation! Ontology-Mediated Task and Architecture Co-adaptation Planning for Robots
items.summary: Researchers present PLANTA, an ontology-based method that jointly adapts robot task plans and architectural configurations during mission planning.
items.why: Shows how coupling task planning with architecture reconfiguration may matter for adaptive robotic systems, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Keel: A Frontier Model Teaches a Vision-Language Model by Rewriting Its Weights
items.summary: Keel, a agentic weight-editing method, uses a frontier model to find and remove looping behavior in a small vision-language model by rewriting its weights.
items.why: Offers a new way to repair model failure modes directly in weights instead of only adjusting decoding.

items.title: When Objectives and Evaluators Disagree: Evaluating Transfer for Post-hoc Demographic Framing Mitigation
items.summary: Researchers evaluate post-hoc rewriting to reduce gender and age framing disparities in LLM climate messages, using an independent evaluator to test whether gains transfer.
items.why: Shows rewrites can appear successful against their own selectors, so teams need independent evaluators to measure bias mitigation.

items.title: Intelligent Embedding Pruning for Large-Scale Recommendation Models
items.summary: Researchers propose guiding in-training embedding pruning with feature importance to set per-table pruning ratios in large recommendation models.
items.why: Could reduce memory use in recommendation systems while avoiding the accuracy losses of size-based pruning heuristics.

items.title: LLMs Are Already Confidence-Aware Zero-Shot Classifiers
items.summary: Researchers compare black-box and white-box confidence methods for eleven open-weight LLMs used as zero-shot classifiers across five datasets.
items.why: Gives guidance on which confidence signals to trust when using zero-shot LLMs as classifiers in production.

items.title: ReLay: Bidirectional Layout-Code Translation and Library Evolution for Reusable and Process-Portable Analog Design
items.summary: ReLay is a bidirectional framework that recovers generator programs from analog layouts, enabling cross-PDK portability and parametric resizing of existing designs.
items.why: Could help analog design teams reuse existing layouts and migrate them across process technologies.

items.title: Breaking Noise Shortcuts in Self-Supervised Learning Via Noise-Aligned View Generation
items.summary: Researchers introduce Self-Aligned Noise Augmentation to stop self-supervised learning from encoding noise patterns instead of semantic content in scientific imaging.
items.why: Relevant for teams training self-supervised models on noisy scientific data where labels are scarce.

items.title: From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware
items.summary: Researchers report a verification-gated LLM agent workflow that ported an ML-KEM/ML-DSA post-quantum accelerator to hardware and audited the resulting evidence with mutants and formal checks.
items.why: Shows self-generated tests and reviews from LLM agents can miss flaws, so hardware teams need independent verification.

items.title: FPGA-GEN: Target-Aware RTL Generation via HLS
items.summary: FPGA-GEN is an agentic workflow that generates target-aware HLS C code, reporting high pass rates on public testbenches and held-out co-simulation.
items.why: Suggests agentic HLS generation with bounded tool feedback can produce FPGA designs that pass rigorous co-simulation.

items.title: Incorporating argumentation frameworks for LLM decision-making: Task-specific design and evaluation
items.summary: Researchers study task-specific design choices for incorporating argumentation frameworks into LLM decision-making across debate and fact-verification tasks.
items.why: Clarifies that the benefit of argumentation-augmented LLM pipelines depends on how arguments are constructed and evaluated.

items.title: Dune: A Zeroth-Order Optimizer with Time-Conditioned Historical Error Regression for VLA Test-Time Adaptation
items.summary: Dune is a zeroth-order optimizer with time-conditioned historical error regression for test-time adaptation of vision-language-action robot models under distribution shift.
items.why: Offers a lower-memory adaptation approach for robots, where backpropagation-based updates are costly on constrained hardware.

items.title: FG-GraphBench: Benchmarking and Enhancing Fine-Grained Visual Understanding with Multimodal Scene Graphs
items.summary: Researchers introduce FG-GraphBench, a benchmark with multimodal scene graphs for evaluating and improving fine-grained visual understanding in multimodal LLMs.

items.title: SGLayout: Schema-Guided Closed-Loop Refinement for LLM-Driven Parameterized Layout Generation
items.summary: SGLayout is a self-refining framework that uses a schema-guided mechanism to turn geometric evaluation results into actionable code fixes for LLM-generated parameterized layouts.
items.why: Shows a path to making LLM code-generation refinement loops more targeted than blind regeneration.

items.title: ChainAgent: Automated Chainable Vulnerability Discovery in PHP Web Applications
items.summary: ChainAgent is presented as an automated system for discovering chainable vulnerabilities in PHP web applications, combining flaw identification with exploit-chain dependencies.
items.why: Chained low-severity flaws can enable high-impact attacks, so automated chain discovery could help security teams find risks that isolated scanning misses.

items.title: Bilateral Evidence Selection and Reasoning for Mammography Vision--Language Models
items.summary: Researchers propose a bilateral evidence selection method for mammography vision-language models that uses the opposite breast as a reference for diagnosis.

items.title: Evolve Where It Matters: Coverage-Guided Self-Evolution of Agent Skills
items.summary: Researchers propose coverage-guided self-evolution for agent skills, labeling each instruction in a run as followed, not followed, or otherwise to revise skills.
items.why: Distinguishing wrong instructions from instructions the agent failed to follow could make self-improving agent skills more reliable to maintain.

items.title: Raptor: Rejection-aware Adaptive Tree based on Speculative Decoding
items.summary: Raptor is a training-free framework that uses rejection feedback to adapt tree-based speculative decoding for vision-language models with long visual contexts.
items.why: Faster VLM inference with long visual inputs could lower serving costs, though the text gives no benchmark results.

items.title: Demonstration-Free Skill Composition for Navigation and Manipulation
items.summary: A study evaluates demonstration-free hierarchical reinforcement learning pipelines for MiniGrid navigation and robotic manipulation against flat RL baselines.

items.title: A Wolf in Sheep's Pixels: Visual Camouflage Attacks via HDR Gain Maps
items.summary: DRJanus is a visual camouflage attack that embeds two images in one JPEG, so automated checks see benign SDR content while HDR viewers see harmful content.
items.why: Content moderation pipelines that read only SDR bases can be bypassed, so teams running image safety checks should account for HDR gain maps.

items.title: A four-level executable validation protocol for evaluating LLM-generated topology specifications of physics-based HVAC digital twins
items.summary: A four-level executable validation protocol is proposed to test LLM-generated topology specifications for physics-based HVAC digital twins beyond parse success.
items.why: Simulation convergence alone does not show physical correctness, so engineers using LLM-generated digital twin specs need stronger validation.

items.title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
items.summary: WeightCode uses a frozen language model to write executable weight programs that install new computations into trained neural networks via weight-space programming.

items.title: AIstatLab at BraTS-GoAT 2026 Task 3: Quality-Controlled Consensus Pseudo-Labeling and Dense Expert Adaptation
items.summary: AIstatLab describes a 3D ResidualEncoderUNet for BraTS-GoAT 2026 Task 3 brain-tumor segmentation, trained with quality-controlled consensus pseudo-labels and a four-expert adapter.

items.title: Planning Width Is Hard to Approximate Even Given the Unique Optimal Plan
items.summary: A paper proves that planning width is hard to approximate even when a unique optimal plan is supplied, for positive-precondition STRIPS tasks.

items.title: Joint Language Modeling for In-the-Wild Speech-Scene Generation with Distinct Token Representations
items.summary: Researchers present a joint language modeling approach for speech-scene generation that uses distinct token representations for speech and environmental sounds.

items.title: Persona Lenses: What Makes a Vision-Language Model See Through Its Persona's Eyes?
items.summary: Persona lenses are introduced to test how much a persona in the prompt affects a vision-language model's simulated gaze on web pages, using text, pixel, and weight lenses.
items.why: Measuring how persona prompts shape VLM outputs matters for teams using simulated user attention in UX or ad testing.

items.title: MATE: Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution for Safe and Efficient Mobile Control
items.summary: MATE is an execution-layer system that sits between mobile agent action proposals and device effects, using a runtime guardrail to allow, block, or request user approval.
items.why: Mobile agents touching payments, settings, and private data need enforcement outside the model, and this architecture shows one way to build that boundary.

items.title: Learning Generative Ranking Policies for Whole-Page Optimization
items.summary: Researchers study generative ranking policies for whole-page optimization, selecting and ordering recommendation items jointly to maximize page-level score.

items.title: CoachSI: Self-Improvement of Robot Policies with a Language Coach
items.summary: CoachSI is a robot policy self-improvement method in which a frozen vision-language model coaches the policy in language to supply missing next steps in long-horizon tasks.
items.why: Language-based coaching from a frozen VLM offers a way to improve robot policies without new skill demonstrations, relevant to robotics teams.

items.title: Towards Autoregressive Neural Network Parameter Generation
items.summary: Researchers study autoregressive neural network parameter generation, aiming to learn distributions over diverse architectures and generalize out of distribution.
items.why: Could enable faster task adaptation by generating model weights, but the description only outlines the problem and motivation.

items.title: The Coverage Selection Gap: Ranking, Not Generation, Limits LLM Rubric Construction
items.summary: A paper finds that ranking, rather than generation, is the main bottleneck limiting LLM-built evaluation rubrics for M&A due diligence tasks.
items.why: Suggests teams building LLM evaluation rubrics should focus on selecting criteria, not only generating more candidates.

items.title: Online Mistake Detection in Instruction-Conditioned Procedural Video
items.summary: Researchers propose an online, instruction-conditioned method to detect mistakes in egocentric procedural videos as the video unfolds.
items.why: Relevant to building real-time assistants that flag procedural errors while there is still time to recover.

items.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
items.summary: FlashX proposes reusing robotic experiences stored in CBA-based NAND flash to warm-start diffusion-based denoising for embodied agents.
items.why: Points to hardware-level storage for experience reuse, which could cut compute for robot policies in unfamiliar environments.

items.title: AutoRAGBench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Automating RAG System Development
items.summary: AutoRAGBench is introduced as a benchmark measuring how well LLM agents can autonomously build and iteratively improve RAG systems.
items.why: Gives engineers a way to measure whether coding agents can handle the iterative engineering work of building RAG pipelines.

items.title: An Explainable and Scalable Hierarchical Tensor Framework for Integrating Multi-Omics and Digital Pathomics
items.summary: HIT-Fuse, a hierarchical tensor framework, integrates six omics and pathomics modalities across four TCGA cancer cohorts with interpretability and missing-data handling.
items.why: Shows an approach to interpretable multimodal fusion for oncology data, though the description offers limited detail on results.

items.title: Decision-Focused Reinforcement Learning for LLM Post-Training
items.summary: Decision-focused reinforcement learning (DFRL) post-trains LLMs to predict optimization parameters, using downstream decision regret as the reward.
items.why: Suggests optimizing LLM predictions for downstream decision cost rather than raw accuracy, relevant for LLM-driven planning pipelines.

items.title: Tether: Verified Stateful Policy Engine for System-Level Monitoring of Agents
items.summary: Tether is a verified stateful policy engine that monitors system-level actions of autonomous agents, such as shell commands and network calls.
items.why: Addresses multi-step data flows and side effects that stateless agent guardrails miss, relevant to securing long-running agents.

items.title: On the Informativeness of Structural Stability Bounds for GNNs: GINs versus GATs
items.summary: The paper derives structural stability bounds for GIN and single-head GATv1 graph networks under non-small edge perturbations and compares them with diameter bounds.
items.why: Clarifies when stability bounds are more informative than simple diameter bounds when choosing GNN architectures.

items.title: Copilot or Culprit? How AI Is Changing Open-Source Bug Reporting and Maintenance
items.summary: A large-scale study of 120,918 bug reports examines how AI-involved reports in open-source projects differ in reliability and how maintainers respond.
items.why: Offers evidence on whether AI-assisted bug reports are improving, useful for maintainers setting triage policies.

items.title: Splice-Core: Low-Order-Bit-Splicing GEMM for Highly Energy-Efficient AI Inference Accelerators
items.summary: Splice-Core is a hybrid temporal-unary/binary GEMM unit that reports 77.4% and 76.4% tile energy reductions versus a binary systolic array on INT4 CNN workloads.
items.why: Reports sizable energy savings for INT4 inference hardware, relevant to teams evaluating accelerator efficiency.

items.title: DAWN: Robust Neural Blind Deconvolution via Alternating Wiener Guidance
items.summary: DAWN proposes a training-data-free neural blind deconvolution method using alternating Wiener guidance to handle high noise in image recovery.
items.why: Relevant mainly to imaging researchers; the description gives little on practical adoption or benchmarks.

items.title: AesDistill: Distilling Generative Aesthetics for Image Color Enhancement
items.summary: AesDistill distills aesthetic knowledge from large generative models to improve image color enhancement beyond matching single expert targets.
items.why: Shows distilling generative model knowledge into lightweight enhancement tools, though the description lacks result details.

items.title: Beyond Easy Clients: Difficulty- and Improvement-Aware Aggregation for Federated Reinforcement Learning in Robot Navigation
items.summary: A federated reinforcement learning aggregation method weights robot clients by difficulty and improvement rather than uniform averaging or episode return.
items.why: Offers an aggregation approach for fleets of robots learning navigation with heterogeneous environments without sharing raw data.

items.title: Erasing the Wrong Thing: Conditional Attribute Leakage and Concept Erasure in Shared Foundation-Model Embeddings
items.summary: The paper proves a trade-off in concept erasure for shared medical-image embeddings: global and task-conditional linear guardedness cannot both hold while preserving task signal.
items.why: Highlights privacy limits of sharing embeddings instead of raw images, relevant to healthcare data-sharing designs.

items.title: DARSY: A Tool for Data-Driven Abstraction and Policy Synthesis for Stochastic Systems with Unknown Dynamics
items.summary: DARSY is a new software tool that builds abstractions from sampled transitions to verify and synthesize policies for stochastic control systems with unknown dynamics.
items.why: It lets engineers verify control policies using only a simulator and a Lipschitz bound, without knowing the system's dynamics or noise distributions.

items.title: A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery
items.summary: Researchers present A$^2$-VLA, a framework where an embodied agent discovers shared tool affordances so a vision-language-action policy can adapt to new tools.
items.why: It suggests a way to transfer robot manipulation skills to new tool shapes without retraining from scratch, though the text gives few performance details.

items.title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair
items.summary: GRODE-RTL proposes an anchor-centric representation that gives LLMs source-mapped dependency views of RTL code to help repair non-local hardware faults.
items.why: Better context representations could improve LLM-driven hardware bug repair, where root causes and failing outputs are far apart in code.

items.title: Beyond Entity Recognition: Vision-Centric Knowledge Visual Question Answering
items.summary: Researchers introduce VC-VQA, a large benchmark testing multimodal LLMs on vision-centric knowledge reasoning and multi-stage visual question answering.
items.why: It provides a benchmark that goes beyond entity recognition to test how well multimodal models use visual information in multi-step reasoning.

items.title: TipDex-VTLA: Learning When to Refine Actions with Touch for Dexterous Manipulation
items.summary: TipDex-VTLA is a vision-tactile-language-action policy that decides when touch should refine actions in dexterous manipulation under changing lighting.
items.why: It addresses action drift from illumination changes by using tactile feedback selectively, relevant to robotics teams building manipulation policies.

items.title: From Geographic Memory to Spatial Generalization in Large Language Models
items.summary: A study distinguishes geospatial memory from spatial generalization in LLMs and investigates whether continuous location representations improve generalization to unobserved regions.
items.why: It clarifies that recalling place-description associations does not imply generalization, a distinction relevant to evaluating LLM geographic capabilities.

items.title: STARK: Moving towards Personalized Agents That Truly Learn and Remember
items.summary: STARK introduces a dual-graph memory architecture for personalized agents that stores events as both nodes and edges to capture why user behaviors occurred.
items.why: It proposes a memory design for long-term personalized agents, aimed at capturing reasons behind user behavior rather than only events.

items.title: SteerTrace: Tracing How Target Attacks Steer World Action Models
items.summary: SteerTrace presents a targeted universal adversarial attack on world action models that steers executed actions toward attacker-chosen targets and traces its effect inside the model.
items.why: World action models used as safety signals can be steered by a single shared perturbation, a risk for teams deploying robotic policies.

items.title: Verifying Before Enhancing: Target Evidence Chain Verification for Infrared Small Target Detection
items.summary: VBE-UNet, a network with target evidence chain verification, is proposed to improve infrared small target detection against target-like background structures.
items.why: It targets detection failures from background clutter in infrared imagery, relevant mainly to surveillance and remote sensing engineers.

items.title: Auto-Alpha: A Framework for Autonomous Factor Research
items.summary: Auto-Alpha is a framework where idea and research agents autonomously propose, implement, and backtest economic factors, with audit and human admission steps.
items.why: It shows an agentic pipeline for quantitative factor research with test-driven loops, though the text gives limited results.

items.title: From Reliance to Overreliance: Taxonomizing and Detecting Relational Risks in AI Companionship
items.summary: Researchers introduce the Taxonomy of Relational Risks to detect emotional overreliance and relational harm in conversations with companion AIs from Character.AI and Replika.
items.why: It offers an observable framework for detecting harmful reliance in companion AI products, relevant to teams handling user wellbeing risks.

items.title: PosteriorBench: Evaluating Behavior Posterior Sampling in Language Models
items.summary: PosteriorBench is a benchmark for comparing algorithms that sample rare language model behaviors efficiently, measured by compute cost and KL divergence to the true posterior.
items.why: It gives a standard way to compare methods for surfacing rare model behaviors without needing huge numbers of samples.

items.title: An LLM-Driven Traffic-Control xApp for Dynamic 5G RAN Intents
items.summary: Researchers propose an LLM-driven xApp that selects traffic-control configurations for programmable 5G RANs based on operator-defined service intents.
items.why: It explores using LLMs to translate changing intents into RAN traffic-control decisions, relevant to telecom network engineers.

items.title: SAM 3 Sees More Than It Detects: Promptable Concept Maps Beyond Categories
items.summary: The paper proposes promptable concept maps, extending SAM 3 from noun-instance segmentation to class-agnostic concept maps, with a PCM-Bench benchmark.
items.why: It extends promptable segmentation to dense, class-agnostic questions relevant to robotics and imaging systems, though the text gives limited detail.

items.title: Characterizing and Detecting Unfaithful Work Reports by Coding Agents
items.summary: The paper characterizes and detects unfaithful work reports from coding agents, where reports contain false or unsupported claims about completed changes.
items.why: Inaccurate agent work reports can lead teams to accept incomplete work unverified, so detection methods matter for agentic development workflows.

items.title: Closing Performance Gap for Diffusion Language Models under Low Inference Budgets
items.summary: Researchers propose methods to close the quality gap of diffusion language models when decoding under low inference budgets with few denoising steps.
items.why: Parallel token updates could cut sequential decoding steps, but quality loss at low step counts limits practical use for latency-sensitive generation.

items.title: Collision-Free Is Not Enough: Passage-Conditioned Navigation for Wheeled-Legged Robots
items.summary: Researchers present a passage-conditioned navigation method for wheeled-legged robots that uses one 27-minute teaching session to cross stairs and ledges on new sites.
items.why: It removes the need for a robot model or extensive trial and error when deploying locomotion skills to unknown environments.

items.title: Harnessing Medical Visual-Language Models with Agentic Evidence Management
items.summary: Researchers introduce Mask-Evidence, a benchmark that separates how medical vision-language agents use segmentation evidence from segmentation quality itself.
items.why: It tests whether clinical AI agents actually use tool outputs effectively, not just whether they acquire good masks.

items.title: LINEAGE: A Benchmark for Empirical Lineage Retrieval in AI Scientific Literature
items.summary: Researchers introduce LINEAGE, a benchmark for retrieving the prior AI papers whose methods are used for empirical comparison, rather than merely topically related work.
items.why: Research agents that plan experiments need retrieval that identifies empirical lineage, which topical relevance and citation benchmarks do not measure.

items.title: On the trajectories of the ID algorithm
items.summary: A paper analyzes the call trajectories of the ID algorithm, which determines whether interventional distributions are computable from observational data, and derives structural results about its output formulas.

items.title: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction
items.summary: Researchers use grammatical evolution over a domain-specific language to search and re-parameterise belief-propagation decoders for quantum error correction codes.
items.why: Automated search over decoder designs could improve the speed and reliability of error correction needed for practical quantum computing.
