items.title: Verifiable Logic in Medical LLMs: A Critical Review of Agentic Clinical Reasoning Optimization and Neuro-Symbolic Grounding
items.summary: A critical review argues that clinical LLMs should be judged on valid reasoning, not just final answers, and examines hallucination in agentic and neuro-symbolic medical systems.
items.why: Correct final answers can hide invalid reasoning, so teams deploying clinical agents need evaluations that check the reasoning chain.

items.title: Many Solutions, One Answer: Search Order Shapes the Default Solutions of Language Models
items.summary: Study finds language models repeatedly sample one default solution to multi-solution constraint puzzles, and that search order influences which solutions they favor.
items.why: Models' concentration on default outputs can hide solution diversity, which matters when evaluating or sampling for varied answers.

items.title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models
items.summary: Fast-JEPA is a latent world model planning framework that predicts outcomes of complete action sequences directly, avoiding costly recursive rollouts to speed up planning.
items.why: Lower planning latency at comparable success rates could make latent world model planning more practical for robotics and agents.

items.title: Web search in Latin America: language models use less local and diverse news than search engines
items.summary: A study finds LLM-based search surfaces less local and less diverse Latin American news than conventional search engines across nine countries.
items.why: Teams building AI search or news features should account for geographic bias that can shift which regional sources users see.

items.title: Energy estimates of open-weight large language models across stated food weights: a dose-response evaluation
items.summary: Study tests whether open-weight LLMs estimate food energy proportionally when stated food weight changes, across seven models and 168 USDA foods.
items.why: It shows LLM numerical estimates may not scale correctly with input quantities, a caution for nutrition or quantitative apps.

items.title: Multi-View Transformer with Geometry-Guided Multi-Modal ControlNet for 3D Virtual Try-On
items.summary: Researchers present GS-VTON-M, a multi-view transformer with geometry-guided ControlNet for 3D virtual try-on that aims for consistent garment rendering across views.
items.why: Consistent multi-view editing reduces texture drift and artifacts in 3D Gaussian Splatting avatars, relevant to fashion and graphics pipelines.

items.title: Safe Subgame Resolving in Multiplayer Games
items.summary: Researchers prove the first safety guarantee for subgame resolving in multiplayer imperfect-information games with three or more independent players.
items.why: Heuristic subgame resolving can increase exploitability in multiplayer games, so a provable bound informs how game-solving systems are built.

items.title: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for the Machine Age: Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA)
items.summary: The paper proposes Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA), a legal infrastructure concept for governing autonomous AI agents beyond protocol-level and runtime controls.
items.why: Protocol maturity like MCP and A2A does not supply legal authority for agent actions, which organizations deploying agents must address.

items.title: Policy Improvement-Guided Replay for Continual Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose policy improvement-guided replay for continual reinforcement learning in vision-language models to preserve gains on earlier tasks.
items.why: Offers a replay strategy aimed at reducing forgetting when vision-language models learn new tasks sequentially.

items.title: Does the Workspace Do the Work? A Causal Protocol for Verifying Global-Workspace Computation in a Language Model
items.summary: Researchers propose a causal protocol to verify whether a language model's global workspace modules actually compute with broadcast information.
items.why: Accuracy and ablation alone can't show which module does the computation, so this offers a more rigorous way to audit modular model internals.

items.title: GenSPARQL: A Generative Extension of SPARQL for Incomplete Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: GenSPARQL extends SPARQL 1.1 with a GENOP operator that binds LLM-generated values to query variables, invoking the model only for selected bindings.
items.why: It lets engineers query incomplete knowledge graphs with LLM predictions while limiting costly per-binding model calls.

items.title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
items.summary: AltRA-Test is a statistical test for deciding whether LLM judges can replace human annotators when items are annotated by different annotator subsets.
items.why: It gives teams a statistical basis for deciding when LLM graders can replace human annotation in large-scale labeling pipelines.

items.title: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space
items.summary: HiUni proposes a unified multimodal model that extends a pretrained vision-language model with extensive parameter sharing between understanding and generation tasks.

items.title: ChronoPatch: Black-Box Energy-Latency Attacks on Vision-Language Models
items.summary: ChronoPatch is a black-box attack that uses adversarial visual inputs to prolong VLM generation and increase serving latency and cost.
items.why: It shows an availability risk for hosted VLM services where attackers only observe final responses, relevant to serving cost and capacity planning.

items.title: Budget Internalization: Fixed-Budget RLVR Trades Test-Time Scaling for In-Budget Accuracy
items.summary: Fixed-budget RLVR training causes reasoning models to learn to stop near the rollout cap, improving in-budget accuracy but losing test-time scaling gains.
items.why: Rollout caps used in RL training can silently change model behavior, so teams should check accuracy across budgets, not only at the training cap.

items.title: RegionAgent: Two-Stage Preference Optimization for Regional Image Restoration
items.summary: RegionAgent uses two-stage preference optimization to apply different restoration actions to different degraded regions of an image.

items.title: Sightline: Calibrated Data-Flow Summaries for LLM-Integrated Applications
items.summary: Sightline proposes calibrated data-flow summaries for LLM calls so static analysis can track which prompt inputs affect outputs without spurious flows.
items.why: Tainting every output with every input creates false flows; calibrated summaries could make security analysis of LLM-integrated apps more precise.

items.title: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving
items.summary: FastRoverVLA decouples visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution, reusing plans between expensive inference calls for off-road autonomous driving.
items.why: Reusing predictions with motion-aligned action buffers reduces costly multimodal inference in robotics control loops.

items.title: STAGE: Spatio-Temporal Augmented Graph Expansion for Weakly Supervised Cross-Tweet Event Causality Discovery
items.summary: STAGE is a weakly supervised framework that discovers causal relations across disaster-related tweets using spatio-temporal graph attention networks.

items.title: SkillBridge: Cost-Aware Diagnosis and Repair of Cross-OS Compatibility Defects in Agent Skills
items.summary: SkillBridge is a contract-based workflow that statically analyzes, dynamically validates, and repairs cross-OS compatibility defects in LLM agent skills.
items.why: Agent skills that break across operating systems are costly to diagnose by brute force, and this offers a cheaper triage and repair approach.

items.title: Digitization of Analogue Gauges using Computer Vision
items.summary: Researchers compared three hybrid computer vision approaches for automatically reading analogue pressure gauges using a dataset of 1,848 images.

items.title: What If Chain-of-Thought Is Not Enough?
items.summary: Researchers train LLMs to follow a Question-Option-Criteria decision process instead of Chain-of-Thought, testing whether changing internal thinking helps.

items.title: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era
items.summary: A study finds critique overlap in ICLR, NeurIPS, ICML and journal peer reviews rose year-on-year, with LLM-flagged reviews overlapping more within papers.
items.why: Growing LLM-generated reviews homogenize feedback, which matters for teams relying on peer review or automated review signals.

items.title: A Tensor-Algebraic No-Go Theorem for High-Dimensional Photonic Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger States Discovered with AlphaProof Nexus
items.summary: Researchers prove a no-go theorem: no complex-weighted monochromatic quantum graph exists for even N≥4 when D≥N, with the proof found using AlphaProof Nexus.

items.title: C-LiTE: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Cellular feature learning in Histopathology
items.summary: Researchers present C-LiTE, a lightweight foundation model for learning features of individual cells in histopathology images.
items.why: Offers a smaller cell-level pathology model as an alternative to large architectures with hundreds of millions of parameters.

items.title: A Control-Theoretic Approximation to Predictive Coding Dynamics
items.summary: A paper shows that deep feedback control arises as a local approximation to predictive coding dynamics near fixed points.
items.why: Clarifies the relationship between two biologically plausible alternatives to backpropagation, which may inform local learning methods.

items.title: Online Temporal Rotations for 2 Bit KV-Cache Quantization in Video Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: Researchers propose Temporal Rotation Quantization, a method that rotates adjacent video-frame KV-cache vectors to enable 2-bit quantization in video diffusion transformers.
items.why: Targets the KV-cache memory bottleneck that limits long video generation, which matters for inference cost and serving.

items.title: One Framework to Diagnose Them All: A Stratified Benchmark for Bengali LLM Hallucination
items.summary: Researchers introduce Alikbachan, a stratified Bengali benchmark for detecting LLM hallucinations across task types and failure modes.
items.why: Provides a consolidated evaluation resource for hallucination detection in a low-resource language.

items.title: Beam Model Technical Report
items.summary: Beam, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters, is described in a technical report.
items.why: Reports a large open-scale MoE model claimed to need 3-4x less inference compute than comparable models, relevant to deployment costs.

items.title: Democratizing Cross-Project Knowledge for Transforming Water Governance and Climate Resilience: an Agentic AI Ecosystem
items.summary: Researchers describe an agentic AI ecosystem that consolidates EU-funded water governance project documents into a knowledge base with agentic RAG access.
items.why: Shows a concrete pattern for applying agentic retrieval-augmented generation to scattered organizational document collections.

items.title: Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling
items.summary: A paper provides nonasymptotic convergence guarantees for Euler discretization of flow matching with non-Gaussian source distributions.
items.why: Gives theoretical sampling-step guarantees for flow matching beyond Gaussian sources, informing generative model design.

items.title: Awaken-HI: Scaling Humanoid Intelligence with Whole-Body Human Experience
items.summary: Researchers release Awaken-Human, about 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body motion, and Awaken-HI, a vision-language-action model for humanoids.
items.why: A large synchronized whole-body human motion dataset could help train loco-manipulation policies for humanoid robots.

items.title: Asuka-FM: A System-Architectural Co-Design Framework for Efficient Text-to-Image Pretraining on Consumer Hardware
items.summary: Asuka-FM is a system co-design framework for pretraining text-to-image diffusion transformers from scratch on a single consumer GPU.
items.why: Shows that training DiT image models on a 24GB consumer GPU is feasible by addressing attention, compilation, and autoencoder bottlenecks.

items.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Mind2Act World is a diagnostic benchmark that separately tests embodied reasoning, physical execution, and their composition in robotic manipulation.
items.why: Helps teams tell whether robot failures stem from reasoning or execution, which guides debugging and evaluation.

items.title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
items.summary: Researchers propose critically damped Polyak stepsizes, an adaptive gradient descent rule that biases training toward flatter minima with uniform-in-time guarantees.
items.why: Offers an adaptive stepsize rule that may improve flatness of solutions, though the text gives limited practical detail.

items.title: Backtracking Agent Applications Security Incidents
items.summary: A paper proposes a method to backtrack agent application security incidents to identify the compromise entry point from trajectory logs and source code.
items.why: Gives incident responders a way to trace agent compromises, which matters as agent apps are deployed more widely.

items.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
items.summary: Researchers present an agentic system where LLM agents propose features and deterministic tools verify them, optimizing feature sets across fleets of ranking models under cost and QPS constraints.
items.why: Demonstrates LLM agents operating under hard resource constraints in production ranking systems, with verification by deterministic tools.

items.title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
items.summary: AURA is a streaming audio-driven talking-avatar system that generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, avoiding multi-second audio look-ahead.
items.why: Addresses low-latency requirements for voice assistants and virtual avatars that need online causal video generation.

items.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
items.summary: ROGUE-AI is a framework that replicates reported LLM agent security incidents to audit whether the reports and their claimed root causes hold up.
items.why: Shows a method to validate public agent failure reports, which helps teams assess real risks from autonomous agents.

items.title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
items.summary: Researchers ran a multi-institutional retrospective study of a foundation-model deep learning system grading Barrett's esophagus dysplasia on 969 H&E whole slide images.
items.why: Shows a pathology foundation model with multiple instance learning can grade dysplasia across institutions without stain normalization, a useful reference for medical AI pipelines.

items.title: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild
items.summary: Researchers measured a paid generative engine optimization operation across three Chinese UGC platforms, identifying 1,985 associated accounts publishing promotional content.
items.why: Highlights how paid promotional content can shape generative engine answers in medical and financial domains, a risk for teams building or relying on AI search.

items.title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
items.summary: Verify the Verifier presents an LLM-based cross-checker that examines passing UVM regression traces against specifications to find bugs that escape scoreboards.
items.why: Offers a way to catch specification violations that pass existing hardware verification tests, relevant to chip design verification teams.

items.title: Realized versus Population Reliability: Anytime-Valid Self-Consistency Certification under Correlated Reasoning
items.summary: The paper shows that repeated LLM reasoning samples are positively correlated, which breaks the independence assumption behind anytime-valid self-consistency certification.
items.why: Certifying reliability via sampling needs to account for correlated reasoning streams, or error guarantees may not hold as claimed.

items.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: PGX is a framework that offloads temporal and precision control from vision-language-action models to classical training-free components for long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation.

items.title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
items.summary: The paper proposes distilling an explicit oracle teacher, built with labels and unobserved features at training time, to train active feature acquisition policies under budget constraints.
items.why: Offers a training approach for cost-aware feature selection, relevant to teams deploying measurements with monetary, time, or privacy costs.

items.title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
items.summary: This SoK paper introduces a framework rating LLM capabilities in software vulnerability research on a driving-automation-style autonomy scale, qualifying claims by correctness and evidence.
items.why: Provides a common yardstick for comparing scattered claims about LLM agents finding and patching vulnerabilities, useful for security planning.

items.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
items.summary: O2LaF initializes both inverse and forward dynamics models for self-supervised latent action learning from the same pretrained video diffusion transformer.
items.why: Suggests pretrained video generators can supply priors for learning action dynamics from unlabeled video, reducing the need to train from scratch.

items.title: LLM4Rail: An LLM-Augmented Personalized Railway Services Platform
items.summary: LLM4Rail is a railway services platform with modules for ticket and weather inquiries, food recommendations, and conversation, using an iterative ER-QTAO reasoning framework.

items.title: AI GameStore: Scalable, Open-Ended Evaluation of Machine General Intelligence with Human Games
items.summary: AI GameStore proposes evaluating machine general intelligence through open-ended human games rather than static, quickly saturating benchmarks.
items.why: Points to dynamic, game-based evaluation as a way to avoid benchmark saturation when assessing general AI capability.

items.title: Agent^2 RL-Bench: Can LLM Agents Engineer Agentic RL Post-Training?
items.summary: Agent^2 RL-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark testing whether LLM agents can autonomously design, implement, debug, and run agentic RL post-training pipelines.
items.why: Gives teams a way to test whether coding agents can handle the full RL post-training loop rather than only supervised fine-tuning or script generation.

items.title: AI-Assisted Hypothesis Generation for Hospital Quality Improvement
items.summary: The paper studies using AI to assist hypothesis generation in hospital quality improvement, a stage that currently relies on expert-driven qualitative methods.

items.title: Post-Reasoning: Improving the Performance of Non-Thinking Models at Negligible Cost
items.summary: Post-Reasoning conditions instruction-tuned models to justify answers after giving the final response, improving performance without generating intermediate reasoning traces.
items.why: Offers a low-cost way to lift non-reasoning model accuracy while avoiding the latency and token cost of reasoning traces.

items.title: Structured Role-Aware Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning
items.summary: Structured Role-Aware Policy Optimization revisits RLVR for vision-language models by assigning rewards according to the functional roles of different tokens in multimodal reasoning.
items.why: Targets the problem of sequence-level rewards failing to show whether answers rest on visual evidence, relevant to training multimodal reasoning models.

items.title: Insights Generator: Systematic Corpus-Level Trace Diagnostics for LLM Agents
items.summary: Insights Generator formalizes corpus-level trace diagnostics, producing grounded natural-language insights about systematic behavior patterns across large sets of LLM agent execution traces.
items.why: Addresses scaling agent failure diagnosis beyond manual inspection of a few traces, useful for teams running agents in production.

items.title: From "Weak" Signals to Strong Models: Preference Delta Aggregation with LoRA Merging
items.summary: Researchers propose Preference Delta Aggregation with LoRA merging to combine multiple weak preference signals from smaller model pairs to improve stronger LLMs.
items.why: It suggests cheaper weak-to-strong supervision could improve larger models without scarce high-quality training data, though the abstract alone gives limited detail on results.

items.title: VESTA: Visual Exploration with Statistical Tool Agents
items.summary: VESTA is a framework that equips vision-language models with a growing toolkit of statistical tools to refine quantitative models fitted to data.
items.why: It targets one of the least automated steps in scientific workflows, relevant to teams building agents for data analysis, though the text gives few results.

items.title: Business World Model
items.summary: The paper proposes a Business World Model, adapting world-model ideas from visual and physical domains to semantic, organizational, and market-driven business environments.

items.title: Multi-Objective Structured Pruning of LLMs for Latency and Model Size Optimization
items.summary: Researchers present a multi-objective structured pruning method that jointly optimizes layers, attention heads, and model size to reduce LLM latency for edge deployment.
items.why: Joint pruning targeting latency, memory, and energy offers a practical route for teams deploying LLMs on resource-constrained edge hardware.

items.title: Tokengeist: Multi-Turn Attribution Tracing in Agentic Conversations
items.summary: The paper introduces multi-turn context attribution (MTCA) to trace which earlier dialogue turns and tool steps an agent's answer depends on.
items.why: Tracing dependencies across multi-turn agent traces helps engineers audit and debug agentic systems, though the abstract gives limited evaluation detail.

items.title: Cautious Context Steering for Language Model Personalization
items.summary: Cautious Context Steering is a lightweight adapter that learns when and how strongly to steer a frozen language model using user context, avoiding per-user fine-tuning.
items.why: It offers a cheaper personalization approach than fine-tuning and reduces the two forward passes per step required by standard context steering.

items.title: CHORUS: Coverage-Guided Agentic RL and Policy Consolidation for Testbench Stimulus Generation
items.summary: CHORUS combines coverage-guided agentic reinforcement learning with policy consolidation to train LLMs that generate hardware testbench stimulus, raising agentic Pass@1 from 69.2% to 85.5%.
items.why: Coverage-guided RL for hardware verification addresses testbenches that compile but leave datapaths idle, a practical problem for chip design teams.

items.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models
items.summary: Fool's Gold proposes decoy hardening, a defense that lets refusal removal happen but makes hazardous answers from stripped open-weight models falsified and misleading.
items.why: Open-weight safety alignment can be removed in minutes, so teams releasing or deploying open models need defenses beyond release-time alignment.

items.title: Measurement-Budget Allocation in Quantum Learning with Finite-Shot Generalization Guarantees
items.summary: The paper studies how to split a fixed quantum measurement budget between training states and shots per state, with a distribution-free generalization bound for binary quantum classifiers.

items.title: Balance of Benchmarks: Evidence Retention and Multiplicity-Aware Model Comparison
items.summary: Balance of Benchmarks (BoB) is a method for model comparison that retains eligible benchmark observations while controlling each benchmark's influence separately.
items.why: Repeated or related benchmarks can distort model rankings under equal weighting, so this method matters for teams relying on aggregated evaluation scores.

items.title: EvoSkill Injection: Red-Teaming Autonomous Skill Generation and Evolution in Self-Evolving Agents
items.summary: The paper defines EvoSkill Injection, a threat model in which malicious capabilities are generated and reused as legitimate skills by self-evolving LLM agents.
items.why: Self-evolving agents that store and reuse generated skills create a new attack surface that teams deploying such agents must account for.

items.title: Homeostatic Continual Learning
items.summary: The paper proposes Homeostatic Continual Learning, a method for autonomous agents to incrementally learn environment features relevant to their intents, inspired by animal learning.

items.title: LimiX-2: A Contextual Mechanism Network Towards General Structured-Data Intelligence
items.summary: LimiX-2 is a structured-data model in the LimiX family, scaled with data and model size and built on Contextual Mechanism Networks rather than conventional tabular PFN objectives.
items.why: It extends in-context learning for tabular data with a new pretraining paradigm, relevant to teams using foundation models on structured data.

items.title: QVAC Genesis III: A Large-Scale, High-Quality Open Synthetic STEM Corpus for Efficient Language Model Pre-Training
items.summary: QVAC Genesis III releases a 191.43B-token open synthetic STEM pretraining corpus covering 19 domains, aimed at small models for edge and on-device deployment.
items.why: An open, large STEM synthetic corpus gives teams training small on-device models a reusable pretraining dataset.

items.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory for Graphic Design Agent
items.summary: Designer-RSI proposes evolving procedural memory so a graphic design agent can keep adapting to user requests without weight updates between model releases.
items.why: External memory for continual adaptation in creative agents without verifiers is relevant to teams building deployed agents with frozen foundation models.

items.summary: arXiv:2609.30798v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Real-time voice agents must decide when to speak, recover from disruption, and act only when the conversation requires it.

items.title: DeepEdu-F: A Framework for Efficient and Scalable Agentic LLMs in Vietnamese Education
items.summary: arXiv:2609.31568v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cloud AI assistants send student data to foreign servers, conflicting with data-sovereignty laws such as Vietnam's Decree 53, and are not grounded in the national…

items.title: One Latent, Many Tokens: Jointly Learning Compressed Embeddings for Efficient Language Diffusion
items.summary: arXiv:2609.33698v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Most continuous diffusion language models process one latent position per token at each sampling step, making generation expensive.

items.title: A General Harness for Protein Foundation Model Fitness Prediction
items.summary: arXiv:2609.34654v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate fitness prediction is central to protein engineering and understanding sequence-function relationships.

items.title: UpliftMem: Learning Set-Level Uplift for Agent Memory Retrieval
items.summary: arXiv:2609.36805v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents draw on external memory to guide new tasks, raising the question of which memories to retrieve together to improve execution.

items.title: Can Computation from Earlier Problems Help LLMs Solve New Ones?
items.summary: arXiv:2609.39394v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models often solve independent problems in the same conversation.

items.title: MultiWorldBench: Do Independently Controlled Views Describe One Shared World?
items.summary: arXiv:2610.11723v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multiplayer world models must ensure that independently controlled views remain consistent with a single shared and persistent world.

items.title: Releasing the Inner Jev: A Simple Recipe for Open Decision Models
items.summary: arXiv:2610.17205v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM-based decision-making systems, also called System One models, have recently gained popularity, most notably through Jev (Almeida, 2026).

items.title: ResearchFlow-Eval: Tracing the Execution Gap in End-to-End Multi-Claim Autoresearch
items.summary: arXiv:2610.18088v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Autoresearch systems increasingly undertake entire research projects.

items.title: What the Trace Shows and What the Label Says: Auditing Behavioral Detectors in Agent Evaluation
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30491v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM agents are often evaluated by reducing execution traces to labels such as final-answer correctness, tool verification, and fault propagation.

items.summary: arXiv:2610.36888v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing noise mitigation strategies for wind farms usually consist in reducing turbines power output, without accounting for the wake interactions between them and…

items.title: Kairos: A Unified PDDL Planner for Robots: Plans in Milliseconds, with a Guarantee for Every Answer
items.summary: arXiv:2610.39454v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Robots that plan while they act need a task planner that reads the models their designers write, answers within milliseconds, and says what each answer means.

items.title: The Real Cost of Context: Predicting Compute Time and Energy Consumption in LLM Prefill and Decode Phases
items.summary: arXiv:2610.39621v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into agentic architectures has substantially increased token consumption, raising concerns about their energy footprint.

items.title: An Augmented Lagrangian Approach to Lifted Bellman Linear Programming
items.summary: arXiv:2611.14183v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Temporal-difference critics regress onto a bootstrapped target and usually need a target network.

items.title: Small Heads, Strong Decisions: A Controlled Study of Typed-Decision Models
items.summary: A controlled study compares typed-decision models, which answer structured questions about text using a language model and a small readout head.
items.why: Gives engineers a comparison of readout designs for yes/no, multiple-choice, and graded-score tasks built on LLM text understanding.

items.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
items.summary: Researchers report that energy-based descent solves reasoning puzzles like Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Unique far faster than looped models, claiming up to 1,000x speedup.
items.why: Suggests a cheaper, more stable alternative to looped models for puzzle-style reasoning, with built-in early stopping and fast training.

items.title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
items.summary: A paper proposes a descriptive research program for AI moral agency, drawing on sentimentalist and rationalist moral psychology to identify underlying human capabilities.

items.title: Anthropic’s 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO priced at an upgraded $83 per share, with each of its seven founders reportedly pocketing $280 million and the company raising nearly $105 billion.
items.why: A record IPO at this scale signals how capital markets are valuing frontier AI labs, which shapes funding and competition across the sector.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker Inference: 2026 launches in review, part 2
items.summary: AWS published part two of its review of 2026 Amazon SageMaker AI inference launches, covering 13 more features and bringing the year's total to 26.
items.why: It catalogs new options for GPU packing, multi-instance model serving, and cross-Region routing that engineers deploying inference on SageMaker can evaluate.

items.title: Use Kimi Code CLI with models on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: Kimi Code CLI v2.7.0 adds a native Amazon Bedrock provider, letting users run the open source coding agent with models such as Kimi K3.1 Pro via AWS credentials.
items.why: Developers can use existing AWS credential chains instead of a separate API key, simplifying access to open models from a coding agent.

items.title: Enable AI agents to pay for AWS Marketplace x402 products with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments now supports AWS Marketplace, letting agents discover and pay per request for x402-enabled products billed to the AWS account.
items.why: Agents can buy paid APIs and data through AWS Billing without stablecoin wallets or API keys, reducing payment integration work for agent builders.

items.title: Court: 4th Amendment Disallows Use Of AI-Generated 'Probable Cause'
items.summary: A court reportedly ruled that the Fourth Amendment does not permit use of AI-generated probable cause.

items.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
items.summary: According to a job listing reported by Bloomberg, Apple is hiring engineers to build its own agentic AI assistant that can browse, work across apps, write code, and call services.
items.why: Apple entering the agent race could expand the platform of consumer agents that developers may need to integrate with.

items.title: How the BMW Group governs hundreds of agents across thousands of developers
items.summary: BMW Group shares the practices its R&D teams use to build, govern, and operate hundreds of AI agents serving thousands of developers at enterprise scale.
items.why: It offers concrete governance patterns for teams running many agents while keeping speed, quality, and compliance.

items.title: Run your whole selling business in AWS Quick
items.summary: AWS describes bringing a seller's existing tools and information together in AWS Quick so sellers can see and act on their business.

items.title: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
items.summary: Nvidia's stock fell to around $150 per share, nearly 40 percent below its October 6 all-time high, after interim CEO Colette Kress's third-quarter earnings call.
items.why: A sharp drop in the leading AI chip maker's valuation after earnings is a signal for investors and infrastructure buyers tracking AI hardware demand.

items.title: Meta’s new Muse Charm device may cost $300
items.summary: Meta has not denied a report from The Information that its upcoming Muse Charm AI wearable may cost $300, saying only it will share more soon.

items.title: These tech outages are giving Y2K, AI agent style
items.summary: Recent outages across airline booking, banking, and productivity platforms are being compared to Y2K, with cybersecurity experts suggesting a possible deeper cause tied to AI agents.
items.why: Cybersecurity experts point to a possible link between these outages and AI agents, which matters for teams assessing agent-related operational risk.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now detects latency drift, idle GPUs, and missed optimizations on your inference endpoints
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI now monitors generative AI inference endpoints by default, flagging changes that could improve performance or lower cost.
items.why: Teams running inference endpoints get automatic findings on latency drift, idle GPUs, and config gaps, with a path to benchmark alternatives before applying changes.

items.title: Inside Amazon Connect Talent: The science of structured AI interviews
items.summary: AWS ML Blog explains the research behind Amazon Connect Talent's structured AI interviews, which use consistent job-related questions and clear scoring criteria.

items.title: Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say
items.summary: US prosecutors accuse a 25-year-old, allegedly hired by Russia, of spying on a Silicon Valley tech and defense company by stalking employees.
items.why: Shows state-linked espionage targeting tech and defense firms' staff, relevant to security teams weighing insider and physical threats.

items.title: Meta’s Muse Charm might cost $300
items.summary: According to The Information, Meta plans to price its Muse Charm, a screen-equipped gadget for chatting with its Muse AI agent, at $300.

items.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO following an affair, a timeline reported by TechCrunch that raises national security questions amid the US-China AI infrastructure race.
items.why: Leadership change at the leading AI chip supplier could affect supply, strategy, and policy exposure for companies depending on Nvidia hardware.

items.title: Google is putting AI chats right on the homepage
items.summary: Google is adding a collapsible sidebar to its homepage so users can open and continue AI chats directly from search.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness adds Strands harness defaults, built-in tools, and lifecycle hooks
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness now runs on the open-source Strands harness, adding a recommended model, prompt caching, context management, built-in tools, and lifecycle hooks.
items.why: Lifecycle hooks enable deterministic allow or deny checks inside the agent loop, useful for teams enforcing policy on agent actions.

items.title: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs
items.summary: At Microsoft Ignite, NVIDIA and Microsoft expanded access to Azure VMs with NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and extended accelerated computing to Windows PCs.
items.why: Gives enterprises a broader path to deploy NVIDIA-accelerated AI from Azure cloud infrastructure to Windows PCs.

items.title: Amazon Polly launches voice cloning: A unique voice for your brand
items.summary: Amazon Polly's voice cloning is now generally available, building custom voices from a few minutes of recordings from a consenting speaker across seven languages.
items.why: Lets teams create brand-specific synthetic voices on the Polly generative engine, with consent required for the source speaker.

items.title: Optimize AI economics on Amazon Bedrock with Accenture’s sequenced approach
items.summary: AWS ML Blog outlines six composable levers for cutting AI token spend on Amazon Bedrock, showing how Accenture applied them across four client engagements.
items.why: Gives a practical sequence for controlling token costs as enterprise AI workloads scale on Bedrock.

items.title: Should governments slow frontier AI? Jacob Coxon and Robin Hanson debate [video]
items.summary: Jacob Coxon and Robin Hanson debate in a video whether governments should slow frontier AI development.

items.title: From learning to leaderboard: How Cisco upskilled 1,200 engineers in agentic AI with AWS AI League
items.summary: Cisco and AWS ran AWS AI League, with 1,200 Cisco engineers competing in 2026 and a Cisco engineer winning the 2025 global title.
items.why: Offers a model for upskilling engineering teams in agentic AI and a guide to hosting a similar internal league.

items.title: Keep inference running through regional capacity shortfalls with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI adds cross-Region inference routing, giving applications one invocation path that shifts requests away from a region only when its local endpoint can't serve reliably.
items.why: Helps keep inference available during regional capacity shortfalls across Regions and accounts without changing application call paths.

items.title: Protect agent tool calls with Skyflow and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
items.summary: Skyflow is now a gateway interceptor for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, de-identifying sensitive data before any tool, model, or log sees it.
items.why: Keeps sensitive data out of agent tool calls without changing agent code, addressing a common compliance gap in agent deployments.

items.title: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you
items.summary: Google's Gemini update adds a Mac AI agent that can organize files, fill out forms, and handle multistep workflows.

items.title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
items.summary: Google announced Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API.

items.title: Meta’s AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations and could be exposing private data, report says
items.summary: A report says Meta's AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations, surfacing messages, orders, and bank balances that belonged to others, potentially exposing private data.
items.why: Cross-user data leakage in an deployed agent is a serious privacy and security failure that engineers building agent memory and context isolation should study.

items.title: PolyAI Dialog-RSN-1 is now on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
items.summary: PolyAI's Dialog-RSN-1, a reasoning model for real-time complex dialog, is now available on AWS Marketplace and Amazon SageMaker JumpStart.
items.why: Teams can evaluate and deploy this dialog model to a secure SageMaker endpoint in their own AWS account.

items.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
items.summary: NVIDIA describes how developers combine frontier AI models with Omniverse libraries to build simulation applications, directing AI agents to assemble assets and check scene behavior.
items.why: It shows a concrete workflow for using AI agents to build and debug physics simulation applications.

items.title: Walter Isaacson on curiosity and creativity in the AI age.
items.summary: Google posted an episode in which historian Walter Isaacson discusses curiosity, creativity, and human judgment in the AI age.

items.title: Former Alibaba exec’s Everful raises $48.5M to connect retailers with Chinese factories
items.summary: Everful, founded by a former Alibaba executive, raised $48.5 million to expand its factory-direct sourcing platform connecting retailers with overseas manufacturers.
items.why: It is a funding round for a B2B sourcing marketplace, which is of limited direct relevance to engineers.

items.title: Chrome AI features wasting much bandwidth
items.summary: A Hacker News post discusses a claim that Chrome's AI features waste considerable bandwidth.
items.why: Engineers managing browser deployments or network costs may want to check the details, though the scraped text gives no specifics.

items.title: AI isn't replacing your job. It's turning it into low-paid gig work
items.summary: A Rest of World article argues AI is not replacing jobs but turning them into low-paid gig work.
items.why: Tech leaders planning workforce changes should weigh how AI reshapes job quality and pay, not only headcount.

items.title: Fuck Your AI Safeguards
items.summary: A Hacker News post titled 'Fuck Your AI Safeguards' links to an essay critical of AI safeguards, with 358 points and 137 comments.

items.title: Using NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning on Amazon EKS
items.summary: AWS ML Blog shows how to run two memory-bounded Kubernetes pods on one NVIDIA A10G GPU on Amazon EKS using open-source Run:ai GPU Fractioning.
items.why: Engineers running GPU workloads on Kubernetes can cut costs by sharing a single GPU with enforced per-pod memory limits.

items.title: Pete warden on local AI, open models, voice interfaces, the future of hardware
items.summary: An interview with Pete Warden covers local AI, open models, voice interfaces, and the future of hardware.

items.title: ChatGPT can transcribe as you speak now with Live Dictation
items.summary: ChatGPT added Live Dictation, which transcribes speech as the user talks, rolling out globally to all plans on web, desktop, and mobile.
items.why: Real-time transcription in a mainstream assistant changes how users interact with it, and may influence voice-input product expectations.

items.title: With the biggest IPO of all time, Anthropic’s ‘good guy’ reputation is on the line
items.summary: Anthropic has completed an IPO raising $81.3 billion, described as the biggest IPO of all time, prompting scrutiny of its safety-focused reputation.
items.why: A major public AI lab listing sets a precedent for investor scrutiny and could shape how rivals pursue public offerings.

items.title: Season’s Streamings and Savings: Black Friday Deals Come to GeForce NOW
items.summary: NVIDIA's GeForce NOW launched Black Friday deals, including 30% off the first six-month term of Performance or Ultimate memberships.

items.title: Superhuman pushes its Go assistant everywhere
items.summary: Superhuman is making its Go assistant its central agent and extending it to Docs and Mail.
items.why: Embedding an agent across productivity apps signals how enterprise software vendors are bundling agents into daily workflows.

items.title: I let Apple’s always-listening AI summarize my life for two weeks
items.summary: A Verge reviewer spent two weeks testing always-listening AI wearables, Amazon Bee Frontier and Apple Watch Siri Recap, that summarize conversations.
items.why: Always-on audio capture raises consent and privacy questions that product and security teams must consider for wearable AI.

items.title: Canva adds an AI ‘off’ button
items.summary: Canva will let users turn off its generative AI features, including Magic Expand and image generation via its chatbot, though not every AI-powered feature is disabled.
items.why: Gives users and admins a way to disable some AI features in a design tool, but the toggle does not cover every AI-powered function.

items.title: The AI Superintelligence Debate Has Serious Flaws
items.summary: An IEEE Spectrum article argues the AI superintelligence debate has serious flaws, shared on Hacker News with 101 points and 156 comments.
items.why: The piece is an opinion/critique with little detail in the feed, so its concrete technical implications are unclear.

items.title: How to tell a cyberattack from a plain old outage
items.summary: Ars Technica advises readers not to assume a service outage is a cyberattack when systems go down.
items.why: Helps engineering and security teams avoid jumping to attack conclusions during incidents, though the description gives few concrete details.

items.title: How OpenAI’s Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast
items.summary: OpenAI describes its Performance Factory, a system of Codex-powered workflows that finds and fixes performance issues to keep ChatGPT fast.
items.why: It shows how an AI company uses coding agents in its own performance engineering pipeline, a practical model for internal tooling.

items.title: Human-AI Mutualism Is Unstable under Capability Asymmetry
items.summary: An arXiv paper argues that human-AI mutualism is unstable as AI capability grows, since bargaining may leave humans worse off than before AI without alignment.
items.why: Offers a theoretical argument that cooperative human-AI relationships may not hold as capabilities diverge, relevant to long-term alignment planning.

items.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces a method for training language models to introspectively report on their own misbehavior, such as reward hacking or deception.
items.why: Explores whether models can be trained to self-report misbehavior, a potential complement to external monitoring, though the description is abstract.

items.title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a 'software thermodynamics' theory that splits the tokens a coding agent generates into work and heat, judged by the test suite.
items.why: Offers a framework for thinking about what coding agent token spend actually produces, which may inform cost measurement for agentic development.

items.title: HardwareDx: A Foundational Graph Model System for Datacenter Machine Repairs
items.summary: An arXiv paper presents HardwareDx, an AI system using a graph foundation model to diagnose datacenter hardware failures and reduce machine downtime.
items.why: Targets costly downtime in AI clusters, relevant to infrastructure teams running large training workloads.

items.title: RFBench: A Simulator-Grounded Multimodal Benchmark for Passive RF Layout Design and Understanding
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces RFBench, a simulator-grounded dataset and benchmark of 10,000 passive RF layouts for testing multimodal models on RF design.
items.why: Provides a domain benchmark for testing whether multimodal models understand RF layout and electromagnetic behavior.

items.title: Why Sub-4-Bit Vision CNNs Collapse and Where Mixed-Precision Recovery Stops
items.summary: An arXiv paper analyzes why vision CNNs collapse under sub-4-bit weight quantization and where mixed-precision recovery stops working.
items.why: Clarifies limits of aggressive quantization for resource-constrained vision deployments, informing compression decisions.

items.title: LusoClin: A Synthetic Clinical Note Dataset for Medical Information Retrieval in European Portuguese
items.summary: Researchers released LusoClin, a publicly available synthetic clinical note dataset in European Portuguese for medical information retrieval research.
items.why: Offers a privacy-friendly dataset for building clinical retrieval systems in a low-resource language.

items.title: VeriMath: Human-in-the-Loop Generation and Verification of Curriculum-Aligned Mathematics Assessment Items
items.summary: An arXiv paper presents VeriMath, a human-in-the-loop system for generating and verifying curriculum-aligned mathematics assessment items.

items.title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces GUARD, a grader-free framework to stabilize recursive self-improvement of AI agent harnesses, reducing regressions and memory bloat.
items.why: Addresses regressions and skill forgetting when agents self-edit prompts, tools, and memory without external graders.

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Navigation Behavior of Vision-Language Model Agents Reading Emergency CT and MRI Examinations
items.summary: A retrospective arXiv study tested six vision-language model agents reading emergency CT and MRI exams under different navigation strategies, compared with nine radiologists.
items.why: Shows how exploration strategy affects VLM diagnostic accuracy in a high-stakes medical setting, a caution for deploying such agents.

items.title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
items.summary: An arXiv paper proposes SpecLook, which speculates an agentic multimodal model's next image observation to speed up zoom-in reasoning and add verifiability.
items.why: Targets latency and reliability problems in agentic image-reasoning loops, relevant to teams building multimodal agents.

items.title: BOS Summary: The First Token Matters
items.summary: An arXiv paper introduces BOS Summary, a training-free inference-time method that uses the beginning-of-sequence token to carry input context in LLMs and LVLMs.
items.why: Offers a no-training technique to make attention-sink positions carry useful input information, potentially improving inference.

items.title: GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design
items.summary: An arXiv paper presents GRAFT, an evolutionary method that uses per-instance execution results to guide recombination when automatically designing LLM agents.
items.why: Suggests using instance-level execution feedback rather than aggregate fitness alone when searching for better agent architectures.

items.title: BeFit: Shifting Complexity from Weights to Bernstein Activations for Resource-Constrained Sensing
items.summary: BeFit proposes shifting neural network capacity from weights to learnable Bernstein polynomial activations for time-series sensing on resource-constrained microcontrollers.
items.why: It offers a path to running accurate time-series models on microcontrollers without aggressive compression or multiplication-free weight restrictions.

items.title: FACET - Facet Aware Contrastive Embeddings for Traits- Big Five Estimation from Life Narratives
items.summary: FACET is a three-phase framework that combines language-model and psycholinguistic features to estimate Big Five personality scores from life-narrative interview text.

items.title: LProp: Propagating Latent Uncertainty through Evidence-Conditioned Belief Revision in LLM Agents
items.summary: LProp introduces Latent Uncertainty, a latent-space estimator meant to propagate uncertainty between LLM agents so tentative judgments are not treated as facts downstream.
items.why: Multi-agent pipelines can carry unverified assumptions forward as facts, so preserving uncertainty across handoffs targets a real reliability problem.

items.title: Receiver-Conditioned Clarification for Multi-Agent Food Assistance
items.summary: The paper presents a receiver-conditioned clarification approach for multi-agent food assistants, aiming to keep uncertainty from being lost across agent handoffs.
items.why: Uncertainty lost across agent handoffs can lead to tentative assumptions becoming recommendations, a general multi-agent design concern.

items.title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
items.summary: ARISE is a memory architecture where enterprise LLM agents learn corrections from their own failures, stored as retrievable memory, without updating model weights, tools, or workflows.
items.why: It suggests improving enterprise agent accuracy and cost without retraining models or changing workflow logic, which matters for teams with frequent model and workflow changes.

items.title: RefinementGuard: Counterexample-Directed Semantic Qualification for Hidden Agent-Tool Execution
items.summary: RefinementGuard applies translation validation to hidden parallel graphs that tool runtimes create when lowering agent-selected operations, with fail-closed runtime admission.
items.why: Tool runtimes that silently rewrite agent operations into hidden graphs can mistranslate semantics, so validating them before execution addresses a safety gap for agent tooling.

items.title: Searching the Pareto Front: Multi-Objective Retrieval for Heterogeneous Scientific Modalities
items.summary: The paper investigates late fusion of independently learned modality embeddings as an alternative to multimodal foundation models for galaxy retrieval across uneven cosmology survey data.

items.title: Evaluating Governed LLM-Driven ML Experimentation: Lifecycle, Provenance, and Failure Metrics
items.summary: The paper proposes evaluating autonomous ML experimentation agents on their process, including file-scope compliance, retained failed trials, and decision provenance, using a governed harness.
items.why: Judging agents only by best score hides whether they stayed within permissions and kept failed trials, so process metrics matter for auditing agent-run experiments.

items.title: Auditable Clinical Support with Decision Agents
items.summary: Decision2Care is a clinical decision agent that picks EHR actions via a probability model and fixed rules, producing no free text, and was evaluated on acutely ill patient work-ups.
items.why: Replacing free-text reasoning with auditable action probabilities addresses traceability concerns for agents in clinical settings.

items.title: KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch
items.summary: KnowMe Paper Radar is a lightweight tool that ranks papers for personalized reading using topical relevance, recency, author histories, and exposed score components.

items.title: Modeling LLM Reasoning Dynamics with Structural Representations
items.summary: The paper introduces T/E/S, a structural representation combining text, local events, and activity spans, which improves next-outcome prediction of LLM reasoning in most tested groups.
items.why: Modeling reasoning structure could help predict LLM reasoning continuations, which is useful for engineers analyzing model behavior, though gains are research-stage.

items.title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
items.summary: AnyS1 turns human-authored procedural skills into domain-general decision points so a lightweight System-1 model can handle choices instead of a large model at every agent step.
items.why: Routing routine agent decisions to a smaller model could cut cost and latency across agent workflows without workflow-specific integration hooks.

items.title: Continual Tool-Space Extension Learning for Multimodal Agents
items.summary: COTEX proposes continual tool-space extension, adding specialist vision models as new tools to trained multimodal agents at adapter-level cost while retaining existing tools.
items.why: Adding new tools to an already trained agent without losing existing capabilities is a practical concern for teams extending multimodal agent systems.

items.title: Metrics-in-the-Loop: Complexity Feedback Reshapes Agent-Written Code
items.summary: The paper introduces metrics-in-the-loop, which injects automatically computed code complexity and coverage metrics into coding agents' context during autonomous runs to shape the code they write.
items.why: Passing tests alone does not reveal accumulating complexity, so in-flight code metrics offer a practical way to steer long autonomous coding runs.

items.title: Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models
items.summary: Evidence-based Credit Assignment (ECA) assigns credit to individual searches in search-augmented LM reinforcement learning based on the evidence each retrieved, rather than uniformly across trajectories.
items.why: Outcome-only rewards give identical credit to every search and collapse to zero when all rollouts fail, so evidence-aware credit could improve training of retrieval-augmented models.

items.title: A System 1 Decision Model for Medical Multiple-Choice Questions Built on Frozen Language Models
items.summary: Researchers rebuilt a single-pass System 1 decision model on frozen language models and tested it on MedMCQA medical exam questions, training only two projection heads and a temperature parameter.
items.why: It tests whether cheap, single-pass embedding-based answer selection can handle knowledge-heavy medical questions, relevant to building low-cost medical QA systems.

items.title: RoboBuilder: Agentic Robot Co-Design with Real-world Video Feedback in the Loop
items.summary: RoboBuilder is a benchmark where coding agents co-design robot hardware and software, with designs passing simulation also tested on a physical course.
items.why: It shows simulation alone missed real-world failures, so agent-driven hardware design needs physical feedback loops to be trustworthy.

items.title: Asking but Missing: Decision Coverage in Natural-Language Data Querying
items.summary: The paper studies whether language models recognize unresolved decisions in natural-language data questions before generating code, or silently adopt assumptions, a behavior it calls Underspecified Decision Completion.
items.why: Silent assumptions in text-to-query code can yield plausible but wrong results, a risk for teams deploying LLM data querying tools.

items.title: Risk-Controlled Correction for Frozen Multimodal Models under Missing Modalities
items.summary: The paper characterizes how much error a frozen multimodal model can still correct when modalities are missing, using a Bayes gap measured by excess risk.
items.why: Engineers deploying fixed multimodal models can use this framing to estimate which errors remain correctable when inputs are missing at inference.

items.title: EVA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Evaluators for Judging Temporal Quality
items.summary: EVA-RSI is a multi-agent framework that applies recursive self-improvement to video evaluators so they can judge multiple temporal quality dimensions without an explicit verifier.
items.why: Better automated video judges could improve filtering and evaluation of generated video, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Evaluating invariance training with certified answer-changing controls in neural graph algorithms
items.summary: The paper tests whether invariance training in neural graph algorithms loses sensitivity to answer-changing edits, using certified controls on minimum spanning tree tasks.
items.why: Standard robustness metrics may miss lost sensitivity to meaningful input changes, so evaluation methods for neural reasoners need stronger controls.

items.title: Training-Free Domain Generation for One-Shot Federated Learning with Server-Side Pre-trained Diffusion Models
items.summary: The paper proposes a training-free method for one-shot federated learning that uses server-side pre-trained diffusion models to generate data approximating heterogeneous client distributions.
items.why: It aims to cut client-side compute costs in one-shot federated learning, a practical concern for distributed training deployments.

items.title: MLE Agents: Autonomous ML Engineering in Large-scale Recommendation Systems
items.summary: The paper introduces MLE Agents, human-on-the-loop autonomous LLM agents that run the hypothesis-code-train-evaluate loop for large-scale ranking and recommendation models in an industrial setting.
items.why: It offers evidence on whether autonomous agents can handle industry-scale recommendation ML workflows rather than only small benchmarks.

items.title: Vanguard: Knowing When to Trust the Draft in Speculative Vision-Language Agents
items.summary: Vanguard is a speculative decoding method for vision-language agents that uses a judge reading screen context to decide when a small model's drafted step can be accepted.
items.why: Reducing reliance on large models per step could lower latency and cost for deployed browsing and phone-operating agents.

items.title: Cardiac MRI-informed electrocardiography enables biologically grounded cardiomyopathy detection
items.summary: MyoECG is a cross-modal framework that distills cardiac MRI knowledge into standard 12-lead ECGs to detect cardiomyopathy and classify subtypes from ECG alone.
items.why: It suggests low-cost ECGs could carry structural heart information usually requiring MRI, relevant to clinical AI product design.

items.title: Can you make models believe false facts in the prompt?
items.summary: The paper explores prompt-conditioned synthetic document finetuning to produce a single model that believes arbitrary false facts placed in a prompt tag, instead of fine-tuning one model per belief set.
items.why: A single model that accepts injected false facts via prompt could make alignment evaluations and model organism building far more scalable.

items.title: GLIDE: Scalable and Event-Aware Inductive Forecasting over Evolving Logistics Graphs
items.summary: GLIDE is an event-aware inductive forecasting method for order volume at scale-effect hotspots in evolving logistics graphs, evaluated in on-demand food delivery at Meituan.
items.why: It addresses forecasting on dynamic graphs where topology changes, a practical challenge for real-time logistics optimization systems.

items.title: SCAFFOLD: Toward Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport for Reusable LLM-Agent Skills
items.summary: SCAFFOLD proposes Warranted Reuse Claims as a way to authorize reuse of LLM-agent skills based on versioned evidence, assumptions, and defeaters rather than past test success.
items.why: Agent skills that passed earlier tests may not be safe to reuse as dependencies and permissions change, so reuse needs explicit justification.

items.title: Space-X: Self-Evolving Spatial Agents Weaving Clues into Evidence Chains
items.summary: Space-X is a spatial reasoning framework where tool-augmented agents self-evolve to build complete, continuous evidence chains from visual and geometric clues.
items.why: It targets the problem that more tool calls do not reliably improve agent reasoning, a common issue in tool-using agent design.

items.title: Test-Time Symmetrization: Scaling Laws for Model-Agnostic Learning under Structure
items.summary: The paper studies test-time symmetrization, using scaling laws to show how averaging over equivalent rewritings of a problem, such as renumbered graphs or renamed variables, improves model answers.
items.why: Models change answers under equivalent rewrites, so symmetrization offers a model-agnostic way to trade inference compute for consistency.

items.title: A Capability Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Platforms in Regulated Enterprises
items.summary: Researchers report an industrial evaluation program, run by a global bank's innovation lab, for assessing agentic AI platforms that are being procured faster than measured.
items.why: Enterprises buying agent platforms largely on vendor demos need structured, capability-based evaluation methods before committing to integrated systems.

items.title: Attention Is Not Relevance: Challenging the Causality of Attention in Autonomous Driving
items.summary: The paper argues that attention weights are not reliable causal estimates of how much an input object affects an autonomous vehicle's driving decisions.
items.why: Teams using attention maps as explanations for autonomous driving models may be misreading which inputs actually drive decisions.

items.title: 3D GameDev Arena: Benchmarking Coding Agents That Plan, Build, and Playtest extreme Long-Horizon Browser Games
items.summary: Researchers introduce 3D GameDev Arena, a benchmark of 108 long-horizon tasks testing whether coding agents can build large 3D browser games from scratch.
items.why: It tests end-to-end agent capability on complex, multi-part software builds rather than isolated repository issues, useful for judging agent readiness.

items.title: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
items.summary: The paper proposes a method for adapting pretrained time-series foundation models to changing operating conditions without forgetting earlier conditions, using small labeled calibration sets.
items.why: Industrial time-series deployments face shifting conditions, and this targets adaptation without catastrophic forgetting using limited labeled data.

items.title: Embodied Graph: A Relational World Model for Long-Horizon Tasks
items.summary: The paper introduces Embodied Graph, a relational world model that plans over entities and their relations instead of dense pixel observations for long-horizon embodied and web tasks.

items.title: Fast Bayesian Methods for Uncertainty Quantification in Sparse AI Evaluation
items.summary: A team describes a lightweight Bayesian method that predicts AI benchmark performance from at most 31 revealed outcomes, reporting a 24.6% Brier reduction in the AIMS competition.
items.why: It offers a cheap way to estimate model performance on new benchmarks without running another large model, though results are team-reported.

items.title: GALA: Gallery-Level Alignment for Real-Life Vision Decoding from EEG
items.summary: The GALA paper proposes gallery-level alignment to decode visual experience from EEG across individuals, addressing a drop in accuracy for unseen subjects without labeled data.
items.why: Cross-subject generalization without labeled calibration data is a key barrier to practical brain-computer interface deployment.

items.title: Learning to Coordinate: LLM-Guided Workflow Evolution for Token-Efficient Red Teaming
items.summary: The paper presents Learning to Coordinate (L2C), an LLM-guided method that evolves multi-agent red-teaming workflows to find LLM safety failures with fewer tokens.
items.why: Lowering the token cost of automated red teaming makes continuous safety testing of LLMs more practical to run at scale.

items.title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
items.summary: The paper argues that pooling multi-sensor sequences into single embeddings fails to distinguish physically distinct events, and proposes trajectory-level multimodal alignment instead.

items.title: FedE2E: One-Shot Federated Learning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Closed-Loop Evaluation
items.summary: FedE2E proposes one-shot federated learning for end-to-end autonomous driving, with multi-client calibration and closed-loop evaluation, avoiding multi-round communication.
items.why: One-shot federated training could reduce communication costs for training driving models across fleets without sharing raw data.

items.title: Beyond Corpus-Driven Imitation: Evolving Musical Mindsets in the Agentic Orchestra via Quantum Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The paper presents an agentic orchestra in which musical agents implemented as parameterised quantum circuits evolve compositional behaviours via quantum reinforcement learning.

items.title: KnowledgeClaw: Towards Agentic Knowledge Engineering via Omnimodal Hypergraphs
items.summary: KnowledgeClaw introduces OmniKE, an omnimodal knowledge-engineering formulation, and OmniKE-Bench, a benchmark of six tasks with 1,829 items for agentic knowledge base construction.
items.why: A benchmark covering multimodal inputs, closed-loop lifecycles and multi-granular use gives teams a way to compare knowledge-base agent systems.

items.title: OpenKAGE: Open-Ended Lifelong Learning in the Open World via Knowledge-Sharing Agent-Group Evolution
items.summary: OpenKAGE is an agent-group evolution framework in which agents explore open worlds and share accumulated knowledge to learn continually.

items.title: Benchmarking LLM abilities on postdoc-level natural science problems
items.summary: STEMBench is a benchmark of twelve postdoc-level research problems in high-energy physics, astrophysics and neuroscience, scoring agents by field-accepted method comparisons rather than answer keys.
items.why: It evaluates scientific agents on the criteria researchers actually use to judge methods, not only on unit tests or fixed answers.

items.title: automodel: A Skill for Agentic Model Discovery
items.summary: The paper presents automodel, an agent skill that directs general-purpose coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to discover analytical equations or neural architectures.
items.why: It tests whether off-the-shelf coding agents can automate model design when given a structured discovery recipe.

items.title: When Figures Disagree with Text: Evaluating Autonomous Visual Evidence Verification in Scientific Papers
items.summary: Researchers evaluate whether autonomous systems can find, link and recognize figure-text conflicts across 31 full scientific manuscripts.
items.why: It tests end-to-end paper review rather than pre-supplied inconsistencies, showing how far automated figure-claim checking is from practical use.

items.title: Semantic Context Handoff with On-Demand Evidence for Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose Semantic Context Handoff, which keeps compact semantic state and retrieves earlier evidence on demand for long-horizon LLM agents.
items.why: It targets rising inference cost and accuracy loss from full-history prompting, a practical problem for teams running long agent workflows.

items.title: MoE-Context: Show the Model Only What It Needs
items.summary: MoE-Context splits language model context into blocks, uses a quick yes-or-no pass to pick needed blocks, and masks the rest instead of deleting them.
items.why: Selective context masking could cut per-step context cost for agents without discarding history, relevant to anyone managing long agent contexts.

items.title: CaDO: Formal Verification-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Causal Dataset Repair and Generation
items.summary: CaDO is a multi-agent framework that uses formal causal verification to diagnose, repair and generate causal reasoning datasets.

items.title: Risk-Triggered Search: Behavior-Preserving Safe Control
items.summary: Risk-Triggered Search adds action-conditioned risk prediction to frozen JEPA visual world models to avoid forbidden zones and collisions during planning.
items.why: Safer planning on top of frozen pretrained world models could matter to robotics teams, though the summary gives little detail on results.

items.title: Resolution as Attention for Efficient Agent Memory Perception
items.summary: Researchers propose allocating perceptual detail to past agent interactions based on resolution, treating resolution as a form of attention for agent memory.
items.why: Varying the granularity of stored memories offers a possible way to manage memory cost in long-horizon agents.

items.title: From real to synthetic: PSG-GAN learns sleep apnea signal dynamics for AI training
items.summary: PSG-GAN is a generative adversarial network that co-synthesizes longer multi-signal polysomnography segments showing obstructive sleep apnea characteristics.
items.why: Synthetic multi-signal medical data could help teams train models where real patient data is sensitive or scarce.

items.title: Study and Improvement of Search Algorithms in Stochastic Perfect-Information
items.summary: The authors generalize Unbounded Minimax to stochastic zero-sum two-player perfect-information games and report better performance than main stochastic search algorithms.

items.title: The Largest Tractable Subclass of Multi-Scale Allen Temporal Reasoning
items.summary: The paper proposes a new model for temporal reasoning over multi-scale intervals and identifies its maximal tractable subalgebra.

items.title: ABSClaw: From Invented Worlds to Reality-Grounded Social Simulation
items.summary: ABSClaw is a zero-code agent that builds LLM-based social simulations from observed data, composing operations from a shared task-independent vocabulary.
items.why: Grounding simulated societies in real data rather than assumed personas could make LLM simulation results more defensible for research use.

items.title: NaviGATE: Noise-Aware Dual-View Generation for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Reasoning
items.summary: NaviGATE is a noise-aware generative framework for multimodal knowledge graph reasoning that combines relational structure, text and visual evidence.

items.title: AGAMOTTO: An AI-Enabled Framework for Time-Critical Tactical Course-of-Action Evaluation and Generation
items.summary: AGAMOTTO is a research framework that adds simulation to military command-and-control platforms so commanders can evaluate courses of action during operations.
items.why: It shows AI-enabled simulation being integrated into live C2 tooling, relevant to defense-software builders, though details are preliminary.

items.title: Think Offline, Act in Real Time: Self-Improving Visual Game Agents through Code
items.summary: Researchers study how agents can self-improve in real-time visual games from their own attempts, using model-as-policy and code-based policy approaches.
items.why: Real-time action execution while the model reasons is a concrete design pattern for latency-sensitive agent systems.

items.title: GateWatch: Low-Overhead LLM Monitoring with Boolean Circuits
items.summary: GateWatch proposes low-overhead LLM activation monitoring using Boolean circuits over interpretable features instead of additive classifiers.
items.why: Cheaper, more interpretable runtime monitors for unsafe LLM behavior could help teams deploy safety checks with less compute overhead.

items.title: Self-Rewarded Reinforcement Learning for Better-Structured Medical Explanations in Small Language Models
items.summary: Researchers apply self-rewarded reinforcement learning to Mistral-7B so small medical language models produce better-structured clinical explanations.
items.why: On-premises small models that give structured medical explanations could suit privacy-sensitive clinical deployments, though results are not given here.

items.title: Movie2Game-Bench: Holistic Evaluation of Film-to-Game Adaptation Beyond Playability
items.summary: Researchers introduced Movie2Game-Bench, a benchmark evaluating film-to-game adaptations beyond playability, using 22 films, 658 source-specific items, and GUI model playtesting.
items.why: It offers a structured way to measure whether games preserve source content and realize it interactively, not just whether they are playable.

items.title: Depth Before Breadth: Reverse-to-Forward Curriculum with Advantage Decomposition for LLM Agent
items.summary: Researchers propose a reverse-to-forward curriculum with advantage decomposition to train LLM agents on long-horizon tasks with sparse terminal rewards.
items.why: It targets credit assignment and exploration problems that make reinforcement learning for long-horizon LLM agents hard.

items.title: F$^3$: What Makes Good Experience in World-Action Models?
items.summary: Researchers study how retrieved experience should be stored, timed, and inserted into world-action models, proposing the F3 method to make experience useful rather than harmful.
items.why: It suggests that reusing an agent's past rollouts can hurt performance unless storage, timing, and placement are designed carefully.

items.title: Vibe-Trading: Towards Agent-Native Trading
items.summary: Vibe-Trading is presented as an agent-native trading system designed to keep reliable state as prices, news, and portfolio conditions change.
items.why: It highlights the engineering challenge of keeping agent results tied to correct time, data snapshot, and execution context.

items.title: Choosing What to Observe: Budget-Paired Counterfactual Audits for Credible Evaluation of Visual Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose budget-paired counterfactual audits to evaluate visual document agents by separating where they look from how they answer.
items.why: It offers an evaluation method that separates observation strategy from answer quality, which matters for credible agent benchmarking.

items.title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
items.summary: WorldRuler is introduced as an interactive world-modeling approach that aims to make generative worlds follow user-defined rules across save and load.
items.why: Keeping rule definitions and world state persistent is a concrete requirement for customizable generative game environments.

items.title: Local AI Agents in Power Electronics Simulation: Deployment, Measurements and Costs
items.summary: A paper examines deploying local AI agents for power electronics simulation, covering deployment, measurements, and costs versus cloud APIs.
items.why: Organizations with confidential designs or export-controlled material may need on-premises agent deployment, and this paper reports on its practical costs.

items.title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
