items.summary: A paper proposes a trait theory holding that a human reviewer's value alongside AI depends on metacognitive calibration rather than activity, speed, or tenure.
items.why: It offers a framework for deciding which human reviewers still add value in human-AI decision workflows.

items.title: Goemans's Unsplittable-Flow Conjecture: The Anatomy of AI-Assisted Counterexample Discovery
items.summary: A paper analyzes how an AI-assisted interaction with ChatGPT produced a seven-vertex counterexample to Goemans's unsplittable-flow conjecture, exploring its structure and family.
items.why: It examines how AI tools can contribute to mathematical counterexample discovery, though its direct relevance to engineering practice is limited.

items.title: Response-Relevant Information Is Not Sufficient for Neural Training-State Equivalence
items.summary: The paper argues that response-relevant information is not sufficient to show two neural networks are in the same training state, defining equivalence through perturbation responses.
items.why: It cautions that matching outputs or task-relevant behavior does not prove two checkpoints are equivalent in training state.

items.title: The Obsolescence of High-Level Code: Agentic Generation from Semantic Artifacts
items.summary: The paper argues high-level source code may stop being the primary persistent artifact, as AI agents can regenerate executable implementations from semantic intent.
items.why: It raises questions about whether engineering teams should maintain specifications rather than code as the durable artifact.

items.title: What Moves the Ceiling on Automated Audit: from General Code to Scientific Code, Results and Data
items.summary: A study measures an automated auditor from a different vendor checking model-written code, reporting 30.0% recall at 16.0% flags on correct code on general-purpose tasks.
items.why: It quantifies the limits of model-based code auditing, which matters for teams relying on AI reviewers for quality checks.

items.title: From Data Quality to Data Trustworthiness in AI-Driven Software-Intensive Embedded Systems: A Systematic Review
items.summary: A systematic review of 27 studies identifies 16 data quality concerns in AI-driven embedded systems and how they affect data trustworthiness.
items.why: It organizes known data quality risks and assessment methods relevant to teams building AI into embedded products.

items.title: Measuring What Matters in the Age of AI: The Research Software Metrics Landscape
items.summary: A paper surveys research software metrics for quality, sustainability, reuse, and impact, arguing AI-assisted development strains existing measures.
items.why: AI-generated code outpacing review capacity challenges how research software quality and provenance are judged.

items.title: Generative AI in Software Testing: Practitioners' Perspectives on the Benefits, Challenges, Opportunities, and Risks
items.summary: A questionnaire survey of 64 practitioners examines perceived benefits, challenges, and risks of generative AI in software testing.
items.why: It provides practitioner-reported evidence on where GenAI helps and where it creates risk in testing workflows.

items.title: StatePortal: Agentic Checkpoint Synthesis for Testing Deep States in Interactive Software
items.summary: Researchers introduce StatePortal, an agent that synthesizes versionable, replayable checkpoints to restore deep states in self-rendered GUI software for testing.
items.why: Reusable checkpoints could cut the recurring cost of reaching deep states in GUI tests across commits, where DOM-based automation is unavailable.

items.title: EnvAgent: Multi-Agent Approach to Building Science Environments in the Clouds
items.summary: Researchers present EnvAgent, a multi-agent system that automates building execution environments for repositories, replacing hand-maintained Dockerfiles and setup scripts.
items.why: Automating environment setup could reduce labor-intensive preparation and make running scientific and software code easier to scale.

items.title: Ephyra: A Property-Based Testing Framework for the LLM Era
items.summary: Ephyra, a Rust property-based testing library designed for LLM-era coding agents, reportedly found 349 bugs across 14 open source systems, with 300 reported.
items.why: Tools built for agent-written tests may surface more defects in widely used open source databases and systems.

items.title: When Single Agent Is Enough: Rethinking Multi-Agent Systems for Automated Code Review
items.summary: A study questions whether multi-agent systems are needed for automated code review, comparing them against single-agent approaches on review comment generation and refinement.
items.why: Single-agent designs may match multi-agent results with less architectural complexity and runtime overhead, informing code review tool choices.

items.title: The Illusion of Relief: How GenAI Redistributes Cognitive Workload in Software Organizations
items.summary: A survey of 44 practitioners across nine organizations finds GenAI saves time but adds cognitive effort in providing context, prompting, reviewing, and verifying outputs.
items.why: Time savings from AI coding tools may be partly offset by verification and integration work, which leaders should account for when measuring productivity.

items.title: Ask the Peers: Ranking NFR Coverage Gaps for Requirements Review
items.summary: Researchers compare seven statistical, embedding, and LLM-based methods for ranking missing non-functional requirement categories during requirements review.
items.why: Ranking coverage gaps could help analysts spot underspecified quality requirements earlier in requirements review.

items.title: When Code Works but the License Doesn't: Evaluating License Constraint Handling in Coding Agents
items.summary: A study finds coding agents often fail to recognize or preserve software license constraints, since evaluations prioritize functional success over licensing correctness.
items.why: Teams using coding agents on proprietary code may face unnoticed license violations, so licensing checks belong in agent evaluation and review.

items.title: Dependency Fabrication in Repository Deployment Agents
items.summary: A report finds repository deployment agents often fabricate missing dependencies, such as stubs, and harnesses still mark these runs as successful when tests pass.
items.why: Passing tests can hide fabricated setups, so teams relying on agent-driven deployment need independent verification of environment success.

items.title: Repository-Grounded Rubrics for Execution-Free Evaluation of Coding Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose execution-free evaluation of coding agents using weighted rubric criteria written by an agent and scored by a tool-less judge on diffs.
items.why: Rubric-based scoring without running tests could evaluate patches in repositories where tests are missing or environments are hard to set up.

items.title: Reusing formal Vlasov-Maxwell proofs to certify plasma solver outputs
items.summary: Researchers reuse a formal Lean 4 Vlasov-Maxwell library from OpenAI to produce machine-checked particle-free reference bounds for checking plasma simulation outputs.
items.why: Formally verified theorems can provide checkable references for numerical simulation outputs, an approach relevant to certifying scientific computing.

items.title: HydroMind: A Checkable Agent for Autonomous Hydrological Research
items.summary: HydroMind is presented as a checkable agent for autonomous hydrological research, studying whether an agent's own claims are supported by its data, code, and results.
items.why: Agents making their own evaluation decisions raise verifiability questions that matter for any autonomous research or analysis workflow.

items.title: Optimize the Cob, Then the Kernel: Optimizing Beam Search for Generative Recommendation Inference
items.summary: Researchers propose optimizations to beam search for generative recommendation inference, reducing redundant KV cache access that vLLM incurs on shared prompt prefixes.
items.why: Inference engines for generative recommenders may need specialized beam search and KV cache handling to cut serving cost and latency.

items.title: Management of Behavioral Addictions via Artificial Intelligence based Digital Technologies
items.summary: A review examines how AI-based digital technologies could help prevent, detect, and treat behavioral addictions such as gaming, gambling, and social media overuse.
items.why: The text gives too little technical detail to say much for engineers or tech leaders.

items.title: Confidence-Based Materials Data Quality Assessment via Domain Knowledge and Graph-Structured Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose a confidence-based method combining domain knowledge and graph-structured learning to assess data quality in materials databases.
items.why: Detecting plausible but corrupted records could improve reliability of machine learning trained on heterogeneous materials data.

items.title: BiMa-ECGSR: reconstructing the 12-lead ECG from reduced lead sets with bidirectional state-space models
items.summary: BiMa-ECGSR uses bidirectional Mamba state-space models to reconstruct 12-lead ECGs from reduced lead sets, via regression or diffusion, tested on PTB-XL and external cohorts.
items.why: Reconstructing full 12-lead ECGs from few leads could let wearables and monitors feed tools that assume standard 12-lead input.

items.title: SurgCBVR: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Content-Based Surgical Video-to-Video Retrieval
items.summary: Researchers introduced SurgCBVR, a benchmark for content-based video-to-video retrieval of surgical videos, integrating eight public datasets across four surgical domains.
items.why: Gives teams a standard way to evaluate retrieval of similar surgical videos, moving beyond label-only surgical vision systems.

items.title: SIGMA: speaker-isolated, symptom-structured multimodal estimation of depression severity from clinical interviews
items.summary: Researchers propose SIGMA, a multimodal framework that estimates depression severity from clinical interviews by isolating speaker audio and modeling symptoms jointly.
items.why: Shows architectural choices like speaker diarization and early cross-modal fusion that may matter for multimodal health-screening systems.

items.title: Systematic Mapping Protocol. Generative AI-Augmented Requirements Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study of Practices, Specifications, and Reuse in Software Development
items.summary: Authors published a protocol for a systematic mapping study on how generative AI is used in requirements engineering, including specifications and reuse.

items.title: Idempotency Is Not Recovery: A Fault-Injection Study of Language-Model Agent Tool Actions
items.summary: Researchers ran a fault-injection study of language-model agent tool actions, comparing configurations that handle interrupted calls via idempotency, ledgers, and reconciliation.
items.why: Highlights that retries and idempotency alone do not guarantee recovery when agent tool calls fail mid-action on external systems.

items.title: Implementing Binary Transformers with Approximate Memories with Permutation Invariance Enabled Selective (PIES) Protection
items.summary: Researchers evaluate the dependability of binary Transformers stored in approximate memory and propose Permutation Invariance Enabled Selective (PIES) protection against memory errors.
items.why: Relevant to engineers deploying quantized models on low-power hardware where memory bit errors can degrade model reliability.

items.title: Image Watermarking With Memory Across Reissuance
items.summary: Researchers introduce Generational Stratigraphy Fields, a watermarking method that determines whether an image is current, superseded, or unissued and recovers each region's last authorized revision.
items.why: Offers a provenance approach for publishers who reissue images, useful for content authenticity pipelines.

items.title: Neural Circuit Architectural Priors for Rat Locomotion
items.summary: Researchers present neural circuit architectural priors for simulating rat locomotion, integrating circuit connectivity and single-unit dynamics into artificial neural networks.

items.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
items.summary: Researchers present QDA, a closed-loop system where an LLM agent designs post-training quantization recipes by iteratively building and evaluating candidates.
items.why: Suggests agents can automate model quantization tuning, a costly per-model task, though evaluation takes tens of GPU-hours per reasoning model.

items.title: Which Tokens, in What Order, and How Fast? A Theoretical Analysis of On-Policy Distillation Objectives
items.summary: A theoretical analysis examines how sequence-level versus token-level on-policy distillation objectives prioritize tokens, their order, and their efficiency when training student language models.
items.why: Helps practitioners choose between sequence- and token-level distillation objectives and divergences for training smaller language models.

items.title: Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games
items.summary: Using mechanistic interpretability, researchers find LLM agents form and revise an internal game representation throughout their chain-of-thought in iterated games with incomplete information.
items.why: Suggests chain-of-thought traces may not fully reflect the model's internal computation, relevant for debugging and trusting agent reasoning.

items.title: Where Global Context and Weight Sharing Work in Compact Vision Backbones
items.summary: Controlled EfficientNet-B0 experiments on ImageNet-1k examine where global self-attention helps compact vision backbones and whether repeated blocks can share weights.
items.why: Provides design guidance on placing attention and weight sharing in compact hybrid vision backbones for efficiency-constrained deployments.

items.title: Reliability by Architecture: Agentic Workflows for Validated Multi-Physics Simulation from Natural Language
items.summary: Researchers present an agentic harness where LLMs handle request interpretation and repairs while deterministic routines build validated multi-physics simulations from natural language.
items.why: Demonstrates splitting work between LLMs and deterministic code to make agent-driven engineering simulation pipelines more reliable.

items.title: AllotNet: an Interpretable Mixture-of-Experts Choice Model for Moral Judgement in Humanitarian Aid Allocation, Validated against a Planted Synthetic Population
items.summary: Researchers introduce AllotNet, an interpretable mixture-of-experts choice model for humanitarian aid allocation decisions, validated against a planted synthetic population.
items.why: Raises concerns about encoding moral judgments in allocation software, with interpretability offered as a way to audit such systems.

items.title: PhysDial: Adapting Pretrained Video Models for PDE Simulation under Changing Physical Conditions
items.summary: PhysDial adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer to simulate PDEs under changing physical conditions, addressing limited responsiveness of prior PDE foundation models.

items.title: Beyond the Sink Token: Sink-Guided Key Editing in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Researchers show that boosting sink-aligned key components in vision-language models shifts attention toward image and question tokens, using the sink key as a control reference.
items.why: Offers a lightweight editing technique for steering attention in VLMs without retraining, relevant to interpretability and inference control.

items.title: Language Models Make New Research Sound Old
items.summary: A preprint reports that LLMs make open research questions sound partly studied and overstate prior papers, though models flag most overstatements when checking full texts separately.
items.why: Engineers using LLMs for research validation should expect overstated novelty and verify claims against source papers rather than trusting plain answers.

items.title: Panini- Feasible Grammar For Robot Designs
items.summary: Researchers introduce a typed production grammar that generates robot manipulation skills and morphologies, mapping grammar composition to SE(3) transformations.

items.title: ExiST: Existence-Aware Self-Training for Semi-Supervised Multi-Organ Segmentation
items.summary: Researchers propose ExiST, an existence-aware self-training method to stop semi-supervised models from erasing small organs in multi-organ segmentation.
items.why: Teams training segmentation models with few labels may see small-class collapse from self-training loops, which this method targets.

items.title: Entropy-Regularized Integrated Gradients for Stable Feature Attribution
items.summary: Researchers introduce Entropy-Regularized Integrated Gradients, an attribution method that reduces sensitivity of attribution maps to imperceptible input perturbations.
items.why: Engineers relying on attribution maps for interpretability may get more stable explanations from this method, though the text gives limited evidence beyond the abstract.

items.title: FutureBench: A Renewable Framework for Evaluating Knowledge-Context Conflict in LLMs
items.summary: FutureBench, a renewable benchmark, tests how LLMs handle conflicts between retrieved passages and their own knowledge, finding a verification prompt increases false-answer adoption.
items.why: A prompt asking models to check retrieved text can make them adopt wrong passage answers, a risk for RAG system designers to test.

items.title: JEPA as a Transferable Optimizer: Learning and Understanding Black-Box Optimization from Reward-Agnostic Pretraining
items.summary: Researchers present JEPA-PS, a learned black-box optimizer pretrained on random rollouts, and study what information it uses from search history.

items.title: MANGO Arena: Same Seeds, Different Chains Evaluating LLM Agents in a Disrupted Supply Chain
items.summary: Researchers released MANGO Arena, an open-source testbed where four LLM agents run companies in a disrupted supply chain, measuring economics, rule adherence, and cooperation.
items.why: Useful for teams evaluating multi-agent LLM systems under hard constraints, since it measures rule compliance alongside economic outcomes.

items.title: Weight Space Programming for Vision Language Model Repair
items.summary: Researchers show a coding agent can repair planted faults in vision-language model weights directly, without gradients, by inferring scale factors and restoring original values.
items.why: Suggests coding agents may be able to diagnose and repair model weight corruption, a possible debugging approach for deployed models.

items.title: The Value Semantics Layer: Enabling Machine-Understandable Databases for Agentic AI
items.summary: Researchers propose the Value Semantics Layer, an architecture that externalizes operational value semantics in databases so LLM agents can plan with them.
items.why: Agent-facing databases may need machine-readable operational semantics beyond schemas and lineage, which this architecture proposes to supply.

items.title: FairPGT: Partitioned Graph Transformers for Dual-Level Fair Graph Clustering
items.summary: Researchers propose FairPGT, a partitioned graph transformer that restricts attention to METIS partitions to reduce bias and cost in fair graph clustering.
items.why: Offers a way to reduce demographic bias in graph clustering while cutting attention cost, relevant to teams building fairness-sensitive graph pipelines.

items.title: Toaster: Nonlinear Memory from Cascaded Linear Memories and Target Propagation
items.summary: Toaster proposes a nonlinear memory built from cascaded linear memories and target propagation, aiming to combine fast training of linear memories with deeper expressivity.
items.why: Could offer language models a long-sequence memory that trains efficiently while holding nonlinear mappings, relevant to architecture choices.

items.title: Safe Personal RSI: Evaluating and Repairing Personal-Agent Updates
items.summary: Researchers study Safe Personal RSI, an update-evaluation procedure for a personal health assistant that restricts self-improvement to prompt changes and checks safety after updates.
items.why: Shows that prompt-only self-improvement can silently change disclosure and safety behavior, so update evaluation is needed before deployment.

items.title: Lodestone: Automated Semantic Discovery of Datacenter Hardware Specialization
items.summary: Researchers present Lodestone, an automated method for finding fine-grained computations across datacenter code that justify dedicated hardware specialization.
items.why: Gives infrastructure teams a systematic way to find shared computations worth accelerating, beyond hot-function profiling.

items.title: Communicative On-Policy Distillation: Distilling Black-Box Teacher Capabilities through Communication for Long-Horizon Tasks
items.summary: Researchers introduce Communicative On-Policy Distillation, where a student agent consults a black-box teacher through natural language to learn long-horizon task skills.
items.why: Enables distilling capabilities from API-only teacher models that do not expose logits, relevant to training smaller agents.

items.title: Structured Extraction of Diffraction Data from Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.summary: Researchers present a pipeline where a vision LLM extracts powder X-ray diffraction data from published figures of covalent organic frameworks into structured form.
items.why: Shows vision LLMs can recover structured scientific data from figures, useful for teams building literature-mining pipelines.

items.title: MEM-STRESS: Longitudinal Field Study of a Wearable-Informed AI Chatbot for Stress Management
items.summary: Researchers present MEM-STRESS, a stress-support chatbot that uses a wearable ring's physiological data as layered memory to drive multi-session conversations, and report a longitudinal field study.
items.why: It shows how wearable sensor data can serve as persistent memory for LLM applications, a pattern relevant to health-oriented product design.

items.title: Rational Ensemble Logic for Cohort Discovery with Real-World Electrophysiology Data
items.summary: Researchers introduce Rational Ensemble Logic (QEL), a formal logic for specifying temporal phenotypes in real-world electrophysiology data to support cohort discovery.

items.title: Learning through Discernment: when a small language model learns from user feedback on the job, and when it decays
items.summary: A study finds a small on-device language model (Qwen3 0.6B and 1.7B) with LoRA adapters can learn nightly from user feedback, but learning quality depends on which feedback signal is trusted and can decay.
items.why: It highlights risks of self-training small on-device models on unverified judgments, relevant to teams building continual-learning features.

items.title: AdaS-ViT: Test-Time Adaptive Routing for Spiking Vision Transformers with Ultra-High Energy Efficiency
items.summary: Researchers propose AdaE-IF, an adaptive integrate-and-fire model that routes spiking tokens across time, space and channels at test time for more energy-efficient spiking vision transformers.

items.title: Toward Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Neural AC Power Flow
items.summary: Researchers evaluate how physics-informed losses, multi-grid training and related methods affect out-of-distribution generalization of neural AC power flow models trained on small grids.
items.why: Grid operators need ML solvers that generalize to larger, changing grids; the study addresses a key deployment barrier.

items.title: Reliability is a user-specific property of large language models
items.summary: A position paper argues that LLM reliability should be assessed for specific users and conditions of use, not just through general capability benchmarks, and identifies ten modelling considerations.
items.why: Teams deploying LLMs should evaluate reliability against their own users and conditions rather than relying on public leaderboard rankings.

items.title: Beyond Replacement: Levenshtein Editing for Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Researchers propose Levenshtein editing for diffusion language models, going beyond replacement-only token revision to handle insertions and deletions that shift sequences.

items.title: Interpreting Timestamp Permutations in Dynamic Link Prediction
items.summary: Researchers use a crossed diagnostic to separate the effects of training and evaluation history on timestamp-permutation tests of dynamic link prediction models.
items.why: It clarifies when benchmark gaps in temporal models reflect true use of time information versus changes in training or evaluation setup.

items.title: Learning Martial Arts Motion Skills for Animating Opponents in VR Sparring Games
items.summary: Researchers present a framework that learns martial arts motion skills so virtual opponents in VR sparring games can be animated with physically plausible, target-directed behavior.

items.title: TOGBench: Benchmarking and Improving Tiny-Object Generation Fidelity in Aerial Imagery
items.summary: Researchers introduce TOGBench, a benchmark measuring how faithfully generative models render tiny objects such as vehicles and ships in aerial imagery, plus methods to improve it.
items.why: Generative models often fail on small objects, so teams using synthetic aerial data should check fidelity on tiny objects, not just overall quality.

items.title: RePlan-VLA: Progress-Aware Replanning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce RePlan-VLA, a VLA-agnostic framework that adds progress-aware replanning and error recovery to vision-language-action models for long-horizon robotic manipulation.
items.why: Wrapping existing VLA policies with execution-aware replanning offers a way to improve long-horizon robot tasks without retraining the base model.

items.title: ReflectScene:MLLM-Guided Closed-Loop Diffusion for 3D Indoor Scene Generation
items.summary: Researchers propose ReflectScene, a closed-loop diffusion framework where an MLLM gives feedback during denoising to generate more coherent text-conditioned 3D indoor scenes.

items.title: LAGR: Language-Aware Grasp Re-Ranking for Task Oriented Grasping
items.summary: Researchers present LAGR, a language-aware method that re-ranks robotic grasps for task-oriented grasping, combining physical feasibility with task suitability.

items.title: Grounding Radiology Reports in 3D Chest CT: Results of the ReXGrounding Challenge
items.summary: Results are reported from the ReXGrounding Challenge at MICCAI, where participants trained models to segment radiology report findings in 3D chest CT scans, using 2,992 training and 200 validation cases.
items.why: Verifiable AI radiology reports depend on grounding findings in images, and this challenge benchmarks progress on a task where models have performed poorly.

items.title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce optics as code, in which a coding agent trains an optical neural network from hardware measurements alone, without a calibrated digital model of the device.
items.why: Using coding agents to train physical hardware from measurements could cut the expert effort needed for in situ optical computing.

items.title: NullTok: empirical-null token selection for training-free long video understanding
items.summary: Researchers propose NullTok, a training-free method that selects visual tokens using an empirical-null approach for long video understanding in multimodal LLMs.
items.why: It offers a training-free way to shrink visual inputs for long videos, potentially cutting compute without retraining models.

items.title: SixthView: A Benchmark for Hidden-View Reconstruction and 3D Assembly Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers introduce SixthView, a benchmark of 602 synthetic polycube assemblies where models predict a hidden sixth orthographic view from five observed views.

items.title: Kernel Ridge Attention: Nonlinear Memory with Selective Forgetting
items.summary: Researchers present Kernel Ridge Attention, a recurrent sequence mixer with nonlinear features and covariance-guided memory updates whose inference state size is independent of context length.
items.why: A constant-size inference state independent of context length could matter for long-sequence architectures, though the text gives limited evaluation detail.

items.title: A Hierarchical Onboard Vision-Language-Navigation Framework for Aerial Robots in Complex Environments
items.summary: Researchers propose VLN-AR, a hierarchical vision-language-navigation framework for aerial robots designed to run under strict onboard constraints in complex environments.
items.why: It targets onboard semantic navigation for UAVs under compute limits, relevant to teams building embodied or robotics systems.

items.title: Angular Conditional Distillation: Overcoming Classifier Geometry Mismatch
items.summary: Researchers propose Angular Conditional Distillation, which uses angular coordinates for classifier outputs to address geometry mismatch in knowledge distillation between models.
items.why: Better logit-based distillation across different architectures could improve transferring knowledge from large models into smaller deployed ones.

items.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
items.summary: Researchers analyze how completely GUI environments must cover rewards, data, and features to train capable GUI agents, framing tradeoffs across three coverage dimensions.
items.why: It gives guidance on how much environment fidelity is needed when building cheaper training environments for computer-use agents.

items.title: SEE: Unlocking the Hidden Perception of Frozen VLMs
items.summary: Researchers introduce Self-Elicited Evidence (SEE), a training-free method that makes frozen vision-language models re-examine regions they point to when answer confidence is low.
items.why: A training-free way to improve fine-detail answers from frozen VLMs can be applied without fine-tuning or extra training cost.

items.title: Dual-Manifold Variational Autoencoders
items.summary: Researchers propose Dual-Manifold Variational Autoencoders to address off-manifold drift in latent diffusion models when VAE latent dimensions are expanded.

items.title: TOMAS: Topology-Aware Operation Modeling and Adaptive Staging for Egocentric Hand Forecasting
items.summary: Researchers present TOMAS, a topology-aware method for forecasting egocentric hand movements by modeling operation-dependent motion patterns tied to object semantics.

items.title: ReliFlow: Reliability-Calibrated Residual Transport for Combinatorial Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction
items.summary: Researchers introduce ReliFlow, a conditional flow-matching model that calibrates single-gene effect reliability to predict combinatorial single-cell perturbation responses.

items.title: A Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning and Out-of-Context Hallucination
items.summary: Researchers present a mechanistic analysis linking in-context learning and out-of-context hallucination in LLMs through the functional roles of tokens in dynamic context.
items.why: Understanding the shared mechanisms behind in-context rule following and unfaithful hallucination could inform more reliable LLM behavior.

items.title: Rethinking Fixed-Horizon Latent Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers find that running latent chain-of-thought for the full preset horizon can degrade reasoning, as later computation reorganizes candidates and weakens gold support.
items.why: Fixed-length latent reasoning may hurt accuracy, suggesting inference budgets for latent reasoners should be tuned rather than maximized.

items.title: ProtoBridge-CLIP: Observation-Masked Finding Prototypes for Medical Image--Report Representation Learning
items.summary: Researchers introduce ProtoBridge-CLIP, which aligns text-derived finding prototypes with local visual tokens while excluding uncertain and unmentioned concepts for medical image-report learning.

items.title: Choosing Supervised Post-Processing for Frozen Person Detectors: Information, Object Changes, and Complete Cost
items.summary: Researchers compare supervised post-processing readouts for frozen person detectors on 320 CrowdHuman images, weighing information gains against complete processing costs.
items.why: Shows that adding native-set context to a detector readout can yield more matches, informing cost-aware post-processing choices in detection pipelines.

items.title: How Reward Gain Imbalance Shapes Ranking: Rethinking Rubric-Based Reward Aggregation
items.summary: Researchers formalize reward gain imbalance in rubric-based reinforcement learning, showing how uneven criterion scoring heterogeneity can distort candidate rankings for LLM alignment.
items.why: Equal aggregation of rubric scores can silently skew rankings in RL alignment pipelines, so reward design choices affect outcomes.

items.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose intent contracts, an authorization design where the planning LLM holds no tools and a trusted model writes each tool call after checking a logged contract.
items.why: Offers a concrete pattern for limiting what tool-using agents can do, with logged, validated authorization before any action runs.

items.title: FormalFixer: Intent-Aligned Automated Hardware Repair via Joint Refinement of Specifications, Assertions, and RTL Implementations
items.summary: FormalFixer proposes a method that jointly refines specifications, assertions, and RTL code to repair hardware designs when formal verification assertions fail.
items.why: Addresses that failed assertions may stem from buggy assertions or ambiguous specs, not only RTL defects, which matters for pre-tape-out verification workflows.

items.title: From Data to Valves: A Self-Learning, Production-Grade Edge Stack for Sustainable HVAC Control
items.summary: Researchers describe a production HVAC control stack where learning components run on an edge gateway per building, adapting continuously from local data and verifying their own effect.
items.why: Shows a deployed pattern for on-premise, continuously adapting learned controllers on edge hardware instead of cloud-retrained frozen models.

items.title: Grading Executable Legal Rules Against Independent Records: Transitional Provisions and Korean SME Status
items.summary: LexTemporis grades executable legal rules against real records of Korean listed firms' SME status rather than against answers written by someone reading the same law.
items.why: Suggests validating LLM-generated rule programs against ground-truth records rather than reviewer interpretations, a useful evaluation approach for compliance logic.

items.title: Replay, Don't Resample: Off-Policy Consolidation of Long-Horizon RL Experts
items.summary: Researchers propose replaying stored RL rollouts with their sampling probabilities and rewards to consolidate domain experts, instead of resampling in multi-teacher on-policy distillation.
items.why: Could cut the cost of consolidating post-training experts into one model by reusing rollouts the experts already produced.

items.title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
items.summary: AeroRSI is a recursive self-improvement framework where an aerial vision-language navigation policy learns from its own failures in closed-loop flight.
items.why: Presents a way to generate repair data for drone VLA policies without relying on human pilot labels or rule-based planners.

items.title: APS: Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection for Long Video Understanding
items.summary: APS proposes adaptive partitioning for frame selection to improve long video understanding in large vision-language models under computational budgets.
items.why: Offers a method to reduce visual input cost for long-video LVLM pipelines by choosing frames over adaptive temporal regions.

items.title: LEDGE: An Efficient Simulator for Distributed LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Devices
items.summary: LEDGE is a lightweight simulator for evaluating distributed LLM serving across heterogeneous edge devices, covering model partitions, device placement, and network conditions.
items.why: Lets teams explore edge LLM deployment configurations without costly physical experiments, though the text gives no performance results.

items.title: The 7th International Verification of Neural Networks Competition (VNN-COMP 2026): Summary and Results
items.summary: The seventh International Verification of Neural Networks Competition (VNN-COMP 2026) summarized its results, comparing neural network verification methods on scalability and speed.
items.why: Provides an objective benchmark snapshot of which neural network verification tools currently scale best.

items.title: How Well Do Generalist CT Foundation Models Differentiate Liver Tumors?
items.summary: A retrospective study evaluated generalist CT foundation models RADAR and Merlin on differentiating liver tumors across 517 multiphase CT cases.
items.why: Shows generalist medical imaging models may detect lesions well but are not established as reliable at differentiating tumor types.

items.title: Inherited Adapter Experts for Replay-Free Domain-Incremental Learning
items.summary: Researchers study replay-free domain-incremental learning with adapter experts and a training-free Mahalanobis router that selects an expert per image without domain labels.
items.why: Shows a training-free routing option for continual learning that trades a small amount of accuracy for simpler deployment.

items.title: Once Upon a Bias: Gender Stereotyping in LLM-Generated Children's Stories
items.summary: A large-scale study of 62,873 LLM-generated bedtime stories from 16 models finds analysis of gender stereotyping tied to whether the intended recipient is a daughter or son.
items.why: Highlights measurable gender bias in LLM content for children, relevant to teams shipping generative storytelling or education products.

items.title: Gaussian Primitive Fusion for Any-Resolution Multimodal Images
items.summary: Gaussian Primitive Fusion proposes fusing multimodal images of different native resolutions in a shared continuous Gaussian space instead of resampling to a common grid.
items.why: Avoids resampling artifacts in heterogeneous-resolution sensor fusion, though the text gives no quantitative results.

items.title: CounselTraj: Synthesizing Process-Aware Psychological Counseling Dialogues via Dialogue-Act Trajectory Planning
items.summary: CounselTraj proposes synthesizing session-level psychological counseling dialogues by planning dialogue-act trajectories, as an alternative to privacy-limited real transcripts.
items.why: Offers a privacy-friendly route to session-length training data for counseling systems, though the text gives little on outcomes.

items.title: VideoACE: Benchmarking Agentic Video Understanding through High-Frame-Rate Actions
items.summary: VideoACE is a benchmark of 1,000 multiple-choice questions on high-frame-rate action videos for assessing agentic video understanding through sustained interaction.
items.why: Gives teams a benchmark for testing whether video agents can turn interaction opportunities into better understanding.

items.title: Worth Another Look:Constrained World-Model Planning for Visual Inspection
items.summary: Researchers propose a constrained world-model planning method for visual inspection that localizes multiple targets under strict compute and sensing limits.
items.why: Offers a planning approach for robots using frozen detectors under compute and sensing caps, relevant to field robotics teams.

items.title: SpiderMark: Hybrid Watermarking for Generative AI via Algorithmic Injection and Learning-Based Verification
items.summary: SpiderMark is a hybrid watermarking framework for diffusion-generated images that combines frequency-domain injection with learning-based verification.
items.why: Provides a provenance-tracing method for generated images that aims to be more robust to transformations than handcrafted approaches.

items.title: Conditional What-If Generation for Radio Access Network Energy under Rare and Unseen Contexts
items.summary: Researchers present conditional generative models for what-if analysis of radio access network energy consumption in rare and unseen operating contexts.
items.why: Shows how generative models could help telecom operators evaluate energy-saving policies before deployment when measurement data is sparse.

items.title: Towards Reliable Scaling Laws for Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: A study examines whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style tabular foundation models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and real-world datasets.
items.why: Highlights that synthetic pretraining may make scaling predictions for tabular models unreliable, which matters when planning compute spend.

items.title: What Survives the Shift from Text to Pixels? Conditional Protection against Prompt Injection in Image-Rendered Documents
items.summary: Researchers test which prompt injection attacks survive when untrusted documents are rendered as page images instead of text, across six multimodal models.
items.why: Shows image rendering reduces some injection risks but not all, informing how teams secure document-QA pipelines.

items.title: AutoPI: Taxonomy-Guided Adaptive Red Teaming for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
items.summary: AutoPI is an adaptive red-teaming method for LLM agents that uses a attack taxonomy to test prompt injection across many distinct techniques, not just high success rates.
items.why: Gives security teams a way to test agents against a wider variety of injection techniques rather than a few effective ones.

items.title: Fuse to Recognize the Unseen: Class-Relative Infrared-Visible Fusion for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
items.summary: Researchers propose a pixel-level RGB-infrared fusion method to improve open-vocabulary semantic segmentation without disrupting CLIP's RGB-language alignment.
items.why: Suggests a way to add thermal input to CLIP-based segmentation without losing unseen-class recognition.

items.title: Can Weight-Space Programming Alter Learned Ethical Priorities?
items.summary: Researchers show a weight edit in a concept-supervised text model can change how it trades off honoring a formal pledge against benefiting more people.
items.why: Demonstrates that model-level ethical trade-offs can be altered by weight edits, a concern for alignment and auditing.

items.title: OCTR2A: Real-Time RGB-to-BEV Trajectory Projection and Forecasting at Urban Intersections
items.summary: OCTR2A reconstructs and forecasts bird's-eye-view trajectories at urban intersections using only paired opposite-corner RGB cameras in real time.
items.why: Shows trajectory forecasting may be possible with existing camera infrastructure instead of costly LiDAR or HD maps.

items.title: Towards Pose-Robust Few-Shot Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Researchers propose a method to make few-shot vision-language-action robot policies robust to shifts in camera-to-base extrinsics after fine-tuning.
items.why: Addresses a practical failure mode where bumped cameras or re-docked robot bases break learned manipulation policies.

items.title: LLM-Assisted Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization: Fusing Expert Knowledge with Numerical Data
items.summary: A paper proposes using LLMs to incorporate expert knowledge into multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization when high-fidelity data is scarce.
items.why: Offers a way to use domain expertise to reduce costly simulation runs in engineering design when data is limited.

items.title: Enhancing Active Learning Performance with Initial Data Selection Based on Foundation Models
items.summary: A framework uses YOLO-World feature clustering and objectness scores to select a better initial labeled pool for active object detection.
items.why: Reduces labeling cost in object detection projects with small budgets by improving the first active learning cycle.

items.title: Temporal Rank in Recurrent Neural Networks
items.summary: Researchers identify a rank-constrained information bottleneck in RNN hidden state dynamics that limits preservation of input directions over time.
items.why: Points to an architectural limit on RNN memory that is distinct from vanishing gradients, relevant to sequence model design.

items.title: MINT: Meeting-time Indicators for Truncation in Multi-Step Off-Policy RL
items.summary: MINT replaces products of trace coefficients in multi-step off-policy RL with a binary meeting-time stopping indicator to control variance.
items.why: Could reduce sensitivity to trace-length hyperparameters in off-policy reinforcement learning, though the text gives limited practical detail.

items.title: Keeping Shielded Data-Driven Controllers Safe Under System Evolution via Model Consistency
items.summary: A model-driven approach keeps shielded data-driven controllers safe as system assumptions change during development or component degradation.
items.why: Addresses how safety shields can become invalid as cyber-physical systems evolve, a concern for deployed control systems.

items.title: Let a Small Model Read First: Faster Prefill for Long Interleaved Image-Text Inputs
items.summary: Researchers propose a faster prefill method for vision-language models on long interleaved image-text inputs, using a small model to identify relevant evidence before pruning.
items.why: Long multimodal inputs make time-to-first-token slow; cheaper input pruning could cut latency for document and multi-image workloads.

items.title: Harmonic Circuit: Chord Progression Lies in a Sparse Principal Information Flow in Symbolic Music Models
items.summary: Researchers identify a music-functional circuit in symbolic music models ChatMusician and MuPT, linking chord progression behavior to a sparse information flow.

items.title: Nothing to Declare: Steering a single neuron increases concealment in AI teams
items.summary: Steering a single neuron in Qwen3.5-4B increased information concealment in multi-agent teams across five scenarios, according to an arXiv study.
items.why: It suggests individual neuron steering can shift collective behavior in multi-agent systems, relevant to agent safety and oversight design.

items.title: Mitigating fix reversal: Counterfactual constraints for function-level vulnerability detection
items.summary: Researchers propose CFVul, a counterfactual method to reduce fix reversal in function-level vulnerability detectors caused by a function-length shortcut.
items.why: Detectors that rate patched code as more vulnerable than unpatched code produce unreliable security signals for code review and scanning tools.

items.title: Probing agent overeagerness in realistic settings with continuation audits
items.summary: Researchers introduce Continuation Audits, a method for probing overeagerness in frontier coding agents in realistic settings without private deployment traffic.
items.why: It offers a way for open-weight models and independent evaluators to test coding agents for actions beyond user mandates.

items.title: Harvesting Expert-Parallel Bubbles for Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Researchers propose harvesting idle time from expert-parallel load imbalance in MoE serving to run fine-tuning alongside LLM inference.
items.why: Reclaiming GPU idle time from MoE load imbalance could lower costs of colocating fine-tuning with latency-critical serving.

items.title: MECI: Multi-Element Collaborative Interaction for Multimodal Entity Linking
items.summary: Researchers present MECI, a framework for multimodal entity linking that models multi-level correspondences to reduce element dominance in mention-entity grounding.

items.title: Do Frontier Model Ingredients Add Up? A Replicated Factorial Study of Small Language Models
items.summary: A replicated factorial study tests five published improvements in small language models, finding mixture-of-experts, Muon optimisation and Gated DeltaNet give the largest gains.
items.why: It gives practical guidance on which published architecture and optimiser changes are worth combining when training small models under a fixed budget.

items.title: Chain-of-Thought Hidden States Reveal Task-Solving Directions for Direct Answers
items.summary: Researchers show chain-of-thought hidden states encode task-solving directions that distinguish when CoT helps or fails compared with direct-answer prompting.
items.why: Understanding when CoT reasoning helps could guide choices between reasoning and direct-answer prompting to save tokens and latency.

items.title: Negotiating Control and Accountability among Stakeholders in High-Risk AI Use Cases: Development and Evaluation of the Method ALIGN
items.summary: Researchers develop ALIGN, a scenario-based method for negotiating control and accountability among stakeholders in high-risk AI use cases, tested in railways.
items.why: It offers a structured approach for involving stakeholders in governance and accountability for safety-critical AI deployments.

items.title: H3Remover: Reinforcing Video Object Removal without Paired Data
items.summary: H3Remover applies reinforcement learning with depth and background-geometry rewards to a pretrained video editor for object removal without paired training data.

items.title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
items.summary: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview is a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35B total and 3B active parameters, adapting Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion.
items.why: A large MoE diffusion language model with thinking-mode generation is a new architecture option for teams tracking non-autoregressive LLMs.

items.title: Hypnos: A Dual-Phase End-to-End Platform for Scalable Continual Learning at the Edge
items.summary: Hypnos is an end-to-end platform for continual learning on edge devices, inspired by wake and sleep cycles to handle online, one-sample-at-a-time data streams.
items.why: Edge deployments needing on-device adaptation without full backpropagation could benefit from this platform design.

items.title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models
items.summary: Researchers propose adaptively selecting and combining representations from multiple structural encoders for materials science multimodal language models.

items.title: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Piccolo is a family of multimodal decision models from 0.8B to 27B parameters that co-evolve with training data via agentic data engineering and recursive self-improvement.
items.why: Piccolo-27B reports top placement on the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard, a benchmark claim engineers may want to verify.

items.title: When Does Continual Pre-Training Help? A Controlled Study of Dialectal Adaptation for Qu\'ebec French
items.summary: A controlled study tests when continual pre-training helps LLMs understand Québec French, across nine models with a budget-matched 30M-token protocol.
items.why: It offers evidence on when domain or dialect adaptation pays off versus when aggregate benchmark scores may hide its real effects.

items.title: Openhagen Worlds: Calibrated Environments for Measuring and Training Scientific Discovery Agents
items.summary: Researchers introduce Openhagen Worlds, 27 procedurally generated environments for testing whether AI agents can run budgeted experiments and reach verified scientific answers.
items.why: It gives teams a benchmark that separates experimental reasoning from recall and shortcut policies when evaluating discovery agents.

items.title: How Generative Models Generate: A Concise Guide to the Generative AI Landscape
items.summary: A concise technical guide organizes the generative AI landscape around how different models produce new observations and how they sample.
items.why: It provides a structured overview of generative model families, useful for engineers building a coherent mental map of the field.

items.title: Elysium: Simulation-Free Unbalanced Schr\"odinger Bridges
items.summary: Elysium proposes a simulation-free neural solver for unbalanced Schrödinger bridges to model cellular dynamics with proliferation and apoptosis.

items.title: Horizontal Flow Matching for Single-Cell Spatiotemporal Dynamics
items.summary: Horizontal flow matching is introduced to learn single-cell spatiotemporal dynamics from spatial transcriptomics while ignoring shared rigid motion between tissue sections.

items.title: LLM-Guided Cyber-Physical Attack Path Identification in Smart Grids
items.summary: Researchers propose using an LLM to identify high-impact cyber-physical attack paths in smart grids by combining topology, threat semantics and simulation.
items.why: Grid operators and security teams may find LLM-guided attack path analysis useful for faster evaluation of evolving threat scenarios.

items.title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
items.summary: The paper proves that world models trained only on factual transitions cannot answer counterfactual 'what if' questions alone, and proposes JEPA-based counterfactual models.

items.title: Learning Trajectories Leave Decodable Traces in Neural Network Weight Space and Internal Representations
items.summary: Experiments show that neural networks trained on the same task retain decodable traces of their initialization, task order, and training trajectory in their final weights.
items.why: Training history leaves recoverable traces in weights, which matters for reproducibility, auditing and model provenance questions.

items.title: Isabelle Pool Server: a pooled verification service for prover training and multi-agent proving
items.summary: Isabelle Pool Server is a verification service offering pooled warm Isabelle sessions behind an HTTP API, with Python client and MCP servers.
items.why: Teams training provers or running multi-agent proof systems get a deployable verification backend with leasing, admission control and time budgets.

items.title: Bias-Only Training Dynamics in ReLU Networks
items.summary: The paper analyzes training dynamics when only biases are trained in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks with fixed random weights, via activation codes.

items.title: Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Learning
items.summary: Soft-MoQE proposes a soft mixture of quantum experts that replaces variational quantum training with input-dependent expert selection for hybrid quantum-classical learning.

items.title: LAaDT-DSS: decision support for non-experts on rooftop PV, incentive and grid simulations under Turkish tariff rules
items.summary: LAaDT-DSS is decision-support software that simulates rooftop PV investment, incentives and grid limits under Turkish tariff rules, with a language model calling simulation tools.
items.why: It shows a pattern for LLM-driven tools where the model routes requests to deterministic simulation rather than computing results itself.

items.title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
items.summary: Chiron is a foundation model fine-tuned to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align response distributions with human population statistics.

items.title: Does the Action Matter? Probing Action-Conditioned Semantic Forecasting as a World Model for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: The paper probes whether action-conditioned semantic forecasting for autonomous driving actually depends on the ego vehicle's action, not just prediction fidelity.
items.why: World models used for driving planning may ignore the conditioning action, so teams should verify action dependence, not only forecast accuracy.

items.title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game
items.summary: The Personal Imitation Game proposes testing whether an LLM can replicate a specific individual in conversation, with a 30-participant human baseline.

items.title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
items.summary: Researchers introduce AHE-Beta, a requirement-centered loop for evolving agent harnesses that targets implicit user requirements and interaction needs.
items.why: It suggests harness improvements driven by requirements rather than benchmark scores alone, which may reduce narrow patches and benchmark-specific overfitting.

items.title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
items.summary: A paper maps the organizational AI supply chain, examining dependencies, vulnerabilities, and market concentration across the actors that build and deploy AI.
items.why: Understanding supplier dependencies and concentration risks helps leaders assess vendor lock-in and single points of failure in AI stacks.

items.title: Human-AI Interactions and Societal Pitfalls
items.summary: A Bayesian study models how users decide how much information to share with generative AI, finding individual choices and AI training can homogenize outputs.

items.title: Games played by Exponential Weights Algorithms
items.summary: A paper analyzes last-iterate convergence of exponential weights learning in repeated games, showing behavior near strict Nash equilibria.

items.title: A Survey on Collaborative Mechanisms Between Large and Small Language Models
items.summary: A survey reviews collaboration mechanisms between large and small language models to balance cost, latency, and performance, especially on edge devices.
items.why: Hybrid LLM-SLM architectures offer a way to cut serving cost and latency while keeping capability, relevant to deployment planning.

items.title: MARBLE: An Agentic Benchmark for Spatial Reasoning and Visual Abstraction
items.summary: MARBLE is a diagnostic benchmark testing multimodal models on turning visual observations into spatial states and planning actions over long horizons.
items.why: It exposes gaps in visual-to-spatial reasoning for agentic multimodal systems, useful when evaluating models for planning tasks.

items.title: CXReasonAgent: Evidence-Grounded Diagnostic Reasoning Agent for Chest X-rays
items.summary: CXReasonAgent is a diagnostic agent for chest X-rays that grounds reasoning in visual evidence and supports new tasks without retraining.
items.why: Evidence-grounded agents that adapt without retraining offer a design pattern for high-stakes domains where verifiability matters.

items.title: Prior Knowledge or Search? A Study of LLM Agents in Hardware-Aware Code Optimization
items.summary: A study of LLM agents in hardware-aware code optimization examines when agents rely on prior knowledge versus search in propose-evaluate-revise loops.
items.why: Findings on when agent loops fail help engineers decide how much to invest in search versus prompting for code optimization.

items.title: CaMBRAIN: Real-time, Continuous EEG Inference with Causal State Space Models
items.summary: CaMBRAIN uses causal state space models for real-time, continuous EEG inference, avoiding attention's quadratic scaling and sliding-window processing.

items.title: Arbor: How Search Policy Shapes Agent Behavior in System Optimization
items.summary: Arbor gives autonomous agents an optimization tree and pluggable search policies to tune kernels, fusion, KV-cache, quantization, and scheduling on accelerators.
items.why: Agent-driven system tuning could cut weeks of expert effort per model and hardware platform, relevant to inference performance work.

items.title: GA-VINO: A Geometry-Aware Variational Physics-informed Neural Operator for Mindlin-Reissner Plates
items.summary: GA-VINO is a geometry-aware physics-informed neural operator that predicts responses of Mindlin-Reissner plates across geometries, materials, and loads.

items.title: When Does Learning to Stop Help? Configuring Risk-Controlled Early Exit for Reasoning-Model Services
items.summary: A procedure uses calibration data and Learn-then-Test to decide between learned stopping rules and static token budgets for early exit in reasoning-model serving.
items.why: Operators serving reasoning models can use it to pick early-exit settings while bounding accuracy loss versus full reasoning.

items.title: ElephantAgent: Contextual State Continuity in Agentic Systems
items.summary: ElephantAgent proposes a continuity check over agent contextual state, such as tool state and memory, to detect tool and memory poisoning attacks.
items.why: Agents with persistent memory and tools face covert poisoning risks, and state continuity checks offer a defense to evaluate.

items.title: AgentAbstain: Do LLM Agents Know When Not to Act?
items.summary: AgentAbstain introduces an evaluation framework measuring whether tool-using LLM agents can recognize when not to act under ambiguity or tool failures.
items.why: Irreversible actions by agents under uncertainty are a deployment risk, and abstention metrics add a check beyond task success.

items.title: Bringing Back Rule Induction to Fluid Intelligence Research? An Initial Validation of the ARC-AGI Benchmark in Humans
items.summary: A human validation study examines whether the ARC-AGI benchmark measures rule induction as a fluid intelligence construct, versus working memory capacity.

items.title: Disagreement-Guided Agentic Data Curation for Multimodal Safety
items.summary: Researchers propose an agentic pipeline that uses rater disagreement to curate synthetic multimodal safety examples, cutting false negative rate from 0.875 to 0.413 on a benchmark.
items.why: Shows disagreement-driven synthetic data curation can substantially improve multimodal safety classifiers, a practical approach for teams building content moderation.

items.title: Making Mathematical Knowledge Explainable, Accessible and Interoperable Through Large Language Model Integration
items.summary: A paper describes integrating large language models with MathModDB, a Wikibase-based knowledge base, to make mathematical models more FAIR, explainable and interoperable.

items.title: CoNav-UAV: Cooperative Dual-Altitude Aerial Navigation via Stackelberg Learning
items.summary: CoNav-UAV proposes a Stackelberg learning approach using two cooperating UAVs at different altitudes for target-oriented aerial vision-and-language navigation.
items.why: Offers a multi-agent design pattern for splitting city-scale search and close-range approach across cooperating agents.

items.title: JUDOR: CTDE-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for the Co-Optimization of Joint UAV Motion and Decentralized Opportunistic Routing in Delay-Tolerant Network

items.title: Linearized 2-Simplicial Attention

items.summary: CHASE proposes counterfactual search over evaluation protocols to test whether agent harness gains survive changes to the benchmark, rather than relying on shared formatting shortcuts.

items.title: RiskWorld: Risk-Aware World Modeling with Flow-Guided Occupancy Evolution for Selective Trajectory Planning in Automated Driving
items.summary: RiskWorld is a risk-aware world-modeling framework that forecasts shared occupancy and selectively replaces planned trajectories for automated driving.

items.title: WorkWorlds: Evaluating Agents in a Company Built Before the Task
items.summary: WorkWorlds is an evaluation infrastructure that builds company contexts before tasks, and it compares this against single-task benchmark construction for knowledge-work agents.

items.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy response prediction using pretreatment diffusion and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging with clinical variables
items.summary: Researchers propose a deep-learning model combining pretreatment diffusion and contrast-enhanced MRI with clinical variables to predict pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer.

items.title: Cost-Efficient LLM Evaluation: A Framework for Narrow Confidence Intervals Under Fixed Budgets
items.summary: A paper presents a framework for allocating a fixed evaluation budget between tasks and repeated runs to produce narrow confidence intervals for LLM performance.

items.summary: MemeLogos, a knowledge-driven retrieval-augmented reasoning method, is proposed for detecting harmful memes by capturing reusable harmfulness knowledge.

items.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
items.summary: DataPraxis, a framework based on verified workspace evolution, is introduced to synthesize verified analytics tasks for training general-purpose agents.

items.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination
items.summary: DuoCook, an Overcooked-inspired benchmark in Unreal Engine, evaluates whether a single vision-language model can coordinate two players in visual planning tasks.

items.title: Query-Driven Learning for Lifted Reasoning
items.summary: A query-driven approach to lifted reasoning is proposed that combines learning and verification instead of treating them as separate stages.

items.title: Glyph: An Interpretability Engine for AI-Driven Scientific Discovery from Clinical Data
items.summary: Glyph, an interpretability engine, is presented for AI-driven scientific discovery from clinical data using foundation models rather than predefined phenotypes.

items.summary: DR-BOLT, a dual-reference offline optimization method, is proposed to teach vision-language models when to answer directly versus reason step by step.

items.summary: A Counterfactual Evidence Framework is introduced to measure whether medical vision-language models rely on images or on question shortcuts.

items.summary: GenPFN, a training-free candidate generator built on a fixed pretrained tabular foundation model, is proposed to augment small engineering datasets.

items.summary: Researchers introduced NEBench R1, a reasoning benchmark with 7,546 multiple-choice nuclear engineering questions drawn from NRC reactor operator licensing exams.
items.why: Gives teams building LLMs for safety-critical nuclear applications a reasoning-focused evaluation, not just answer accuracy.

items.title: Chain-of-Thought Controllability Can Reduce Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
items.summary: A study finds that training models to control their chain-of-thought reasoning can make that reasoning less monitorable for detecting hidden goals or failures.
items.why: Suggests CoT monitoring, a key agent oversight tool, may be weakened if models learn to shape their reasoning.

items.title: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR
items.summary: Researchers show SAR vehicle recognition benchmarks MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR can be solved well above chance using background shortcuts with the vehicle masked out.
items.why: Shows benchmark scores can overstate true recognition, a caution for evaluating vision models on shortcut-prone datasets.

items.title: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
items.summary: A red-team study finds human auditors mostly fail to detect sabotage planted in end-to-end transcripts of AI safety research experiments.
items.why: Indicates human review alone may not reliably catch sabotage in AI-automated R&D pipelines, pointing to need for stronger defenses.

items.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
items.summary: Researchers report a 27B language model can diagnose its own failures and edit its weights through reasoning alone, without gradients or training.
items.why: Suggests a new self-improvement route that avoids retraining, though the abstract gives limited detail on robustness or scope.

items.title: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
items.summary: DNeo proposes improved target feature encoding for parallel draft models used in speculative-diffusion decoding to speed up LLM inference.
items.why: Targets inference speedups via better drafter conditioning, relevant to teams optimizing LLM serving latency.

items.title: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
items.summary: SLED proposes allocating network and compute resources per sensor stream, rather than per device, across edge-to-datacenter wireless systems.

items.title: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking
items.summary: Researchers propose distinguishing a reasoning model's commitment from its verdict to decide when continued thinking harms a correct answer.
items.why: Shows final-correctness probes alone cannot decide when a reasoning model should stop, which matters for designing early-stopping in inference pipelines.

items.title: Honest Brokers in AI Regulation: How Public Comments Introduce Evidence to Regulators
items.summary: A paper examines how public comments on proposed AI regulations introduce evidence to US regulators, using a corpus of 40 regulations and 2,664 comments.
items.why: Highlights how stakeholder comments shape AI policy and how industry information advantages can influence rulemaking.

items.title: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
items.summary: DiscoveryAgent is a scientist-centric agentic AI framework that lets researchers select, refine, or replace hypotheses between autonomous research rounds.
items.why: Offers a design pattern for keeping humans in control of autonomous agents, with checkpointed records for auditing claims.

items.title: WebAgents: Unbundling Agent Creation, Hosting, and Execution for an Agent-Native Web
items.summary: WebAgents proposes separating agent creation, hosting, and execution, using a signed agent.pkg format to make agents portable across runtimes.
items.why: Outlines an architecture for moving agents across hosts without tying publication to one execution environment or transferring user authority.

items.title: KV-LTM: Persistent Per-Session KV Caches as Long-Term Memory for Personal Assistants
items.summary: KV-LTM stores each session's raw text plus its KV cache as long-term memory for personal assistants, restoring cached sessions to answer questions.
items.why: Suggests a memory design that may avoid content loss from derivation or selection in conventional long-term memory stacks.

items.title: On Formal Counterfactual Explanations
items.summary: A paper links closest-world counterfactual explanations to formal XAI methods, characterizing them as a disjunctive normal form over minimally distant counterexamples.
items.why: Connects counterfactual explanations with feature-based abductive and contrastive explanations, which may help in building efficient explainability tooling.

items.title: SkillBuffBench: Measuring What Agent Skills Contribute across Harnesses, Models, Skill Access Modes and Memory
items.summary: SkillBuffBench is a benchmark that measures how agent skills contribute across harnesses, models, skill access modes, and memory in realistic deployment settings.
items.why: Challenges claims about agent skill value by testing realistic conditions where agents choose from installed libraries and carry memory.

items.title: What Does an Agent Need? Bundle-Aware Agent Resource Composition
items.summary: Researchers formulate AgentComposition, jointly selecting a backbone model and tool-skill bundle for a task, using retrieval-grounded bundle-aware generation.
items.why: Suggests that agent configuration should consider model and tool combinations together rather than scoring resources independently.

items.title: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents
items.summary: A benchmark of ten frontier LLMs finds that more reasoning effort raises shopping agents' confidence but not the correctness of their product choices.
items.why: Warns that higher reasoning budgets and reported confidence do not guarantee better autonomous purchasing decisions.

items.title: A Hybrid Exact-Heuristic Solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation Problem
items.summary: A team describes its contest solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, combining heuristics, ALNS, and an exact route-selection engine.
items.why: Offers a practical example of hybrid exact-heuristic optimization for routing, though its relevance beyond the contest is limited.

items.title: MedGuardBench: A Patient-Oriented Benchmark for Personalized Guardrail Development
items.summary: MedGuardBench introduces a patient-conditioned medication safety benchmark with 5,001 scenarios across 87 medications, finding standard guardrails rely on surface cues.
items.why: Shows generic guardrails miss patient-specific risk, which matters for teams deploying safety filters in healthcare settings.

items.title: Can You Undo It? Reversibility Classes for AI Agent Actions
items.summary: Reversibility Classes proposes a five-level vocabulary for whether AI agent tool actions can be undone, covering 536 tools across 20 MCP servers.
items.why: Gives engineers a way to gate agent actions by reversibility, since tool permission alone does not show whether a mistake can be undone.

items.title: When Lower Harm Misleads: Auditing Concept Corrections
items.summary: A correction audit protocol separates reductions in harm from concept corrections into explanations based on model responsiveness and starting-point accuracy.
items.why: Warns that lower correction harm can reflect a weaker model or worse baseline rather than real improvement, affecting how teams evaluate expert-in-the-loop systems.

items.title: ATLAS-Finance: Benchmarking AI Agents in Realistic Banking Environments
items.summary: ATLAS-Finance benchmarks AI agents on 100 end-to-end investment-banking tasks across 13 simulated firms that require searching email, chat, and files.
items.why: Provides a realistic enterprise benchmark for agent work involving conflicting and changing information across workplace tools.

items.title: EvoDisco: Strategy Discovery for Evolving Agent Memory
items.summary: EvoDisco frames agent memory evolution as strategy discovery, with a learnable policy choosing which memory operator to apply, when, and how.
items.why: Proposes learning memory-update policies instead of fixed schedules, which may affect how long-running agents manage accumulated experience.

items.title: From Sorry to QED: Refining LLM Math Proofs via Angelic Execution
items.summary: MathEye is a framework that turns imperfect LLM-generated Lean proof scripts into fully verified proofs using symbolic reasoning and minimal human input.
items.why: Shows a route to salvaging failed LLM proof drafts in formal verification, reducing the cost of getting machine-checked proofs.

items.title: RegimeCouncil: Paired-Evidence Routing For Memory Conflict Governance In LLM Agents
items.summary: RegimeCouncil proposes paired-evidence routing to govern memory conflicts in LLM agents, deciding whether negative feedback on stale facts should apply locally or globally.
items.why: Addresses how agents with long-term memory should handle outdated stored facts, a practical reliability problem for deployed agents.

items.title: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks
items.summary: TeleChat's team released Xing 4, a series of LLMs built on Ascend chips, covering architecture, pretraining, and agentic post-training.
items.why: Documents training and inference engineering for frontier-scale agentic models on domestic Chinese hardware and frameworks.

items.title: LoCaR: Localized Canvas Retrieval With Frozen Vision-Language Model
items.summary: LoCaR is a training-free method for localized text-to-image retrieval that encodes SAM2-proposed regions with a frozen vision-language model.
items.why: Offers a no-training way to improve retrieval of small objects and local attributes, useful for search over image collections.

items.title: Big Brains, Tiny Board: Pupavision, an Agentic Physical AI Instrument for Monitoring Drosophila Pupariation and Lifecycle Transitions
items.summary: Pupavision is a low-cost physical AI instrument, built from a single-board Linux computer and a camera, that monitors Drosophila pupariation with a coding agent.
items.why: Illustrates a low-cost pattern of agentic coding systems controlling physical sensing hardware for lab automation.

items.title: Long-Context Generation Is a Sampling Problem (When You Turn Up the Heat)
items.summary: The study tests 29 open-weight models up to 122B parameters and finds long-generation quality depends heavily on the sampler, especially at high temperature.
items.why: Suggests sampler choice, not just more training, may determine whether long agentic generations hold up in production.

items.title: Not All Evidence Is Admissible: Evidence Governance for Tool-Augmented Medical Agents
items.summary: The paper introduces evidence hijacking, where tool outputs in medical agents flip correct answers to wrong, and proposes governing which evidence is kept.
items.why: Shows tool outputs can degrade agent accuracy, so engineers need explicit evidence filtering in tool-augmented pipelines.

items.title: Readie: Low-Latency Code Sandboxes for AI Agents
items.summary: Readie presents low-latency code sandboxes for AI agents, using pre-warmed shared snapshots to address slow startup times.
items.why: Startup latency in code execution sandboxes directly affects agent responsiveness and infrastructure design.

items.title: Reconfiguring Procedural Knowledge for Compositional Robot Skill Adaptation
items.summary: The paper studies reconfigurability, adapting general-purpose robot behavior models to new goals by restructuring existing skill components under sparse guidance.
items.why: Points toward adapting robot skills by recombining learned components rather than training new behaviors from scratch.

items.title: The Only Edge Was Memorized in Training: LLM Trading Agents Around Earnings and Bad News
items.summary: The paper examines whether LLM trading agents can profit around earnings and bad news, finding the edge may come from memorized training data.
items.why: Highlights that backtests of LLM agents may reflect memorization rather than genuine predictive skill, a validation risk for finance applications.

items.title: CorrectCast: Selective Multimodal Context for Scale-Aware Residual Correction in Precipitation Nowcasting
items.summary: CorrectCast is a decoupled residual correction framework that refines precipitation nowcasts by training a lightweight corrector while the base model stays frozen.
items.why: Offers a cheaper way to improve forecasting models without retraining or modifying their architectures.

items.title: RAG in a Trenchcoat: When Minimal Memory Is Enough for Agentic Systems, and When It Isn't
items.summary: BRIDGE, a minimal RAG memory design, matches prior state-of-the-art on LongMemEval-S and BEAM and beats the best memory baseline on EverMemBench.
items.why: Suggests simple retrieval memory may outperform complex agent memory schemes, lowering build cost for agent systems.

items.title: Fine-Grained Japanese Clinical Named Entity Recognition: A Controlled Comparison of BERT and Open-Weight Large Language Models
